title.zh: 卷六十 列傳第四十八: 李弼 宇文貴 侯莫陳崇 王雄
title.en: Volume 60 Biographies 48: Li Bi, Yu Wengui, Houmo Chenchong, Wang Xiong
title.raw: 卷六十 列傳第四十八: 李弼 宇文貴 侯莫陳崇 王雄 Volume 60 Biographies 48: Li Bi, Yu Wengui, Houmo Chenchong, Wang Xiong

sentences.zh: 李弼 宇文貴 侯莫陳崇 王雄

translations.literal: Li Bi, Yuwen Gui, Houmo Chenchong, Wang Xiong
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi, Yuwen Gui, Houmo Chenchong, and Wang Xiong

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十八

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Forty-Eight
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 48

sentences.zh: 李弼曾孫密宇文貴子忻愷侯莫陳崇子穎崇兄順王雄子謙

translations.literal: Li Bi's great-grandson Mi; Yuwen Gui's sons Xin and Kai; Houmo Chenchong's son Ying and Chenchong's elder brother Shun; Wang Xiong's son Qian
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi, great-grandson of Li Bi; Yuwen Xin and Yuwen Kai, sons of Yuwen Gui; Houmo Ying, son of Houmo Chenchong, and Houmo Shun, Chenchong's elder brother; Wang Qian, son of Wang Xiong

sentences.zh: 李弼，字景和，隴西成紀人。

translations.literal: Li Bi, styled Jinghe, was a man of Longxi Chenji.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi, courtesy name Jinghe, was from Chenji in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 六世祖振，慕容垂黃門郎。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Zhen was a Yellow Gate Gentleman under Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Zhen had served Murong Chui as a Yellow Gate Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 父永，魏太中大夫，贈涼州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yong was a Grand Master of Palace Attendants of Wei and was posthumously made Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yong had been a Grand Master of Palace Attendants under Wei and was posthumously enfeoffed as Governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 弼少有大志，膂力過人。

translations.literal: Bi from youth had great ambition, and his physical strength surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Bi nursed great ambitions, and his strength surpassed that of ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 屬魏亂，謂所親曰：「大太夫生世，會須履鋒刃，平寇難，以取功名，安能碌碌依階以求仕。」

translations.literal: When Wei fell into disorder, he said to those close to him: "A true man born into this world must tread sharp blades, pacify bandit troubles, and win merit and fame—how can he drudge along the ranks seeking office?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei realm fell into chaos, he told those close to him, "A true man born into such times must walk amid drawn blades, quell rebellion, and win fame through merit. How could he plod up the ladder of office in dull obscurity?"

sentences.zh: 初為別將，從爾硃天光西討，破赤水蜀，以功封石門縣伯。

translations.literal: At first he served as a separate commander, followed Erzhu Tianguang on the western campaign, defeated the Chishui Shu, and for his merit was enfeoffed as Baron of Shimen County.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as a separate commander under Erzhu Tianguang on the western campaign, defeated the Chishui Shu, and was enfeoffed Baron of Shimen County for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 又與賀拔岳討萬俊醜奴、萬俊道洛、王慶雲，皆破之。

translations.literal: He also joined Heba Yue in attacking Moqi Chounu, Moqi Daoluo, and Wang Qingyun, and defeated them all.
translations.idiomatic: He also campaigned with Heba Yue against Moqi Chounu, Moqi Daoluo, and Wang Qingyun, defeating them all.

sentences.zh: 賊咸畏之曰：「莫當李將軍前也。」

translations.literal: The rebels all feared him and said: "None can stand before General Li."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels all feared him, saying, "No one can stand against General Li."

sentences.zh: 及天光赴洛，弼隸侯莫陳悅，征討屢有克捷。

translations.literal: When Tianguang went to Luoyang, Bi came under Houmo Chenyue and in campaigns repeatedly won victories.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianguang marched to Luoyang, Bi served under Houmo Chenyue and won repeated victories on campaign.

sentences.zh: 及悅害賀拔岳，周文帝自平涼討悅。

translations.literal: When Yue killed Heba Yue, Emperor Wen of Zhou marched from Pingliang to attack Yue.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue murdered Heba Yue, Emperor Wen of Zhou marched from Pingliang to punish him.

sentences.zh: 弼諫悅，令解兵謝之。

translations.literal: Bi remonstrated with Yue, urging him to disband his troops and submit in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Bi urged Yue to disband his army and submit in apology.

sentences.zh: 悅惶惑，計無所出。

translations.literal: Yue was alarmed and confused, with no plan to offer.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was alarmed and at a loss for any plan.

sentences.zh: 弼知悅必敗。

translations.literal: Bi knew Yue would certainly be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Bi knew Yue was doomed to defeat.

sentences.zh: 周文帝至，悅乃棄秦州南出，據險以自固。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou arrived, Yue abandoned Qin Province and marched south, holding defensible terrain to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou arrived, Yue abandoned Qin Province, marched south, and entrenched himself in difficult terrain.

sentences.zh: 是日，弼密通于周文，許背悅。

translations.literal: That day Bi secretly communicated with Emperor Wen and promised to turn against Yue.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Bi secretly contacted Emperor Wen and pledged to betray Yue.

sentences.zh: 至夜，弼乃勒所部，雲悅欲向秦州，命皆裝束。

translations.literal: By night Bi mustered his command, saying Yue intended to march on Qin Province, and ordered all to prepare their gear.
translations.idiomatic: That night Bi mustered his troops, claiming Yue meant to march on Qin Province, and ordered everyone to pack up.

sentences.zh: 弼妻，悅之姨也，時為悅所親委，眾咸信之，人皆散走。

translations.literal: Bi's wife was Yue's maternal aunt and was then trusted by Yue; the men all believed her, and people scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's wife was Yue's aunt and enjoyed Yue's trust; the soldiers believed her, and the men scattered in flight.

sentences.zh: 弼慰輯之，遂擁以歸周文。

translations.literal: Bi comforted and gathered them, then led them in submission to Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Bi rallied and reassured them, then brought them over to Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 悅由此敗。

translations.literal: Yue was thereby defeated.
translations.idiomatic: From this Yue was ruined.

sentences.zh: 周文謂曰：「公與吾同心，天下不足平也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said to him: "If you and I are of one mind, the realm is not hard to pacify."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen told him, "With you and me of one mind, the realm will not long remain unconquered."

sentences.zh: 大統初，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, he was advanced to General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry and Opening Office with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Datong era, he was promoted to General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry and Opening Office with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 從平竇泰，斬獲居多。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Dou Tai, and his beheadings and captures were numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in defeating Dou Tai and won many kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 周文以所乘騅馬及泰所著牟甲賜弼。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou bestowed on Bi the piebald horse he rode and the helmet and armor that Tai had worn.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou bestowed on Bi his own piebald mount and the helmet and armor Dou Tai had worn.

sentences.zh: 又從平弘農。

translations.literal: He also followed in pacifying Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in pacifying Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 與齊神武戰于沙苑，弼軍為敵所乘。

translations.literal: When he fought Qi Shenwu at Shayuan, Bi’s army was pressed by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the battle with Qi Shenwu at Shayuan, Bi’s army was overrun by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 弼將其麾下九十騎橫截之，賊分為二，因大破之。

translations.literal: Bi led ninety cavalry under his command in a crosswise cut through them; the enemy split in two, and he then greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Bi led ninety of his cavalry in a crosswise charge, splitting the enemy in two and routing them.

sentences.zh: 以功進爵趙郡公。

translations.literal: For this merit, his title was advanced to Duke of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement, his title was advanced to Duke of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 四年，從周文東討洛陽，弼為前驅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he followed Emperor Wen of Zhou east to campaign against Luoyang, with Bi serving as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, he followed Emperor Wen of Zhou east against Luoyang, serving as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 東魏將莫多婁貸文率眾至穀城，弼倍道而前進，遣軍士鼓噪，曳柴揚塵。

translations.literal: The Eastern Wei general Moduolou Daiwen led his forces to Gucheng; Bi advanced by forced march, sending soldiers to beat drums and shout and to drag brushwood to raise dust.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Wei general Moduolou Daiwen led troops to Gucheng, Bi advanced by forced march and had his soldiers drum, shout, and drag brushwood to raise dust.

sentences.zh: 貸文以為大軍至，遂走。

translations.literal: Daiwen thought a great army had arrived and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Daiwen thought the main army had arrived and fled.

sentences.zh: 弼追斬貸文，傳首大軍。

translations.literal: Bi pursued and beheaded Daiwen, sending his head to the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Bi pursued Daiwen, beheaded him, and sent the head to the main army.

sentences.zh: 翌日，又從周文與齊神武戰河橋，身被七創，遂為所獲，陽隕絕於地，睨其傍有馬，因躍上得免。

translations.literal: The next day, he again followed Emperor Wen of Zhou in fighting Qi Shenwu at Heqiao; he received seven wounds and was captured, then feigned falling unconscious to the ground, saw a horse nearby from the corner of his eye, and leapt onto it, thereby escaping.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, he again followed Emperor Wen of Zhou in fighting Qi Shenwu at Heqiao. Wounded seven times, he was captured, but feigned collapse on the ground, spotted a horse beside him, leapt onto it, and escaped.

sentences.zh: 歷位司空、太保、柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Minister of Works, Grand Protector, and Pillar of State Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to serve as Minister of Works, Grand Protector, and Pillar of State Grand General.

sentences.zh: 廢帝元年，賜姓徒何氏。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Deposed Emperor, he was granted the surname Tuhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Deposed Emperor, he was granted the surname Tuhe.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜太傅、大司徒。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Grand Mentor and Grand Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Grand Mentor and Grand Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 及晉公護執政，朝之大事，皆與於謹及弼等參議。

translations.literal: When Hu, Duke of Jin, governed, all major affairs of court were discussed jointly with Yu Jin, Bi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Hu, Duke of Jin, held power, all major court affairs were discussed with Yu Jin, Bi, and others.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，除太師，進封趙國公，邑萬戶，前後賞賜巨萬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, Bi was appointed Grand Preceptor, advanced in fief to Duke of Zhao State with ten thousand households, and received enormous rewards before and after.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, Bi was appointed Grand Preceptor and advanced to Duke of Zhao State with a fief of ten thousand households. The rewards he received over time were immense.

sentences.zh: 弼每征討，朝受命，夕便引路，略不問私事，亦未嘗宿於家。

translations.literal: Whenever Bi went on campaign, if he received orders in the morning, by evening he had already set out; he paid almost no attention to private affairs and never once slept at home.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Bi campaigned, if he received orders in the morning, he set out by evening, paying almost no attention to private affairs and never sleeping at home.

sentences.zh: 兼性沈雅，有深識，故能以功名終。

translations.literal: Moreover, his nature was calm and refined, and he had deep discernment; therefore he was able to end with achievement and reputation intact.
translations.idiomatic: He was also calm and refined by nature, with deep judgment, and so was able to preserve his achievements and reputation to the end.

sentences.zh: 薨於位，明帝即日舉哀，比葬，三臨其喪。

translations.literal: He died in office; Emperor Ming held mourning that same day, and before the burial, personally visited the funeral three times.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office. Emperor Ming held mourning that very day and personally visited the funeral three times before the burial.

sentences.zh: 發卒穿塚，給大路、龍旗，陳軍至墓。

translations.literal: Soldiers were dispatched to dig the tomb, and he was supplied with the grand carriage and dragon banners, with troops arrayed to the grave.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers were sent to dig the tomb; he was provided the grand carriage and dragon banners, and troops were arrayed all the way to the grave.

sentences.zh: 諡曰武。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Wu.

sentences.zh: 尋追封魏國公，配食文帝廟庭。

translations.literal: Soon he was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Wei State and was paired for sacrifice in Emperor Wen’s ancestral temple court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Wei State and given a place in sacrifice in Emperor Wen’s temple court.

sentences.zh: 子曜居長，以次子暉尚文帝女義安長公主，故遂以為嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yao was the eldest, but because the second son Hui married Emperor Wen's daughter, the Princess of Chang of Yi'an, Hui was therefore made heir.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Yao, but because the second son, Hui, married Emperor Wen's daughter, the Princess of Chang of Yi'an, Hui was made heir instead.

sentences.zh: 初賜爵義城郡公，嘗臥疾期年，文帝憂之，賜錢一千萬，供其藥石之費。

translations.literal: At first he was granted the title Duke of Yicheng Commandery. Once he lay ill for a full year; Emperor Wen worried for him and granted ten million in cash for his medicines.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed Duke of Yicheng Commandery. When he once lay ill for a full year, Emperor Wen, anxious for him, granted ten million cash to cover his medical expenses.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei, he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of the Office with the same ceremonial rank as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry with the status of a Grand Master of the Office equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 出為岐州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 從文帝西巡，率公卿子弟別為一軍。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Wen on a western tour and led the sons of ministers and nobles as a separate army.
translations.idiomatic: On Emperor Wen's western tour he commanded a separate force made up of the sons of high officials.

sentences.zh: 後襲趙國公，改襲魏國公。

translations.literal: Later he inherited the title Duke of Zhao, then had it changed to Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He later inherited the title Duke of Zhao, which was then changed to Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 天和六年，進位柱國。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhe he was advanced to Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianhe he was promoted to Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 建德元年，出為梁州總管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiande he went out as Commander-in-Chief of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiande he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 時渠、蓬二州生獠積年侵暴，至州綏撫，並來歸附。

translations.literal: At that time the raw tribes of Qu and Peng had for years raided and plundered; when he reached the province he pacified them, and they all came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal peoples of Qu and Peng Provinces had raided the region for years; once he arrived and pacified them, they all submitted.

sentences.zh: 璽書勞之。

translations.literal: An imperial letter commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent him an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 暉弟衍，字拔豆，少專武藝，慨慷有志略。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother Yan, styled Badou, from youth devoted himself to martial arts and was bold and generous with ambition and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger brother Yan, courtesy name Badou, devoted himself to martial arts from youth and was bold, generous, and full of strategic ambition.

sentences.zh: 仕周，為義州刺史，封真鄉公。

translations.literal: He served Zhou as Governor of Yi Province and was enfeoffed Duke of Zhenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he served as Governor of Yi Province and was enfeoffed Duke of Zhenxiang.

sentences.zh: 王謙作亂，以行軍總管從梁睿擊平之，進上大將軍。

translations.literal: When Wang Qian rebelled, he served as Campaign Commander under Liang Rui and helped crush the revolt, and was promoted to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Qian rebelled, he served as campaign commander under Liang Rui, helped put down the revolt, and was promoted to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇元年，以行軍總管討平叛蠻，進位柱國。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang under Sui, as Campaign Commander he suppressed rebellious tribes and was advanced to Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang under Sui he served as campaign commander, suppressed rebellious tribes, and was promoted to Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 後拜安州總管，以疾還京，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of An Province, returned to the capital on account of illness, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Commander-in-Chief of An Province, returned to the capital because of illness, and died there.

sentences.zh: 子仲威嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhongwei succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongwei succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 衍弟綸，最知名，有文武才用。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Lun was the most renowned and possessed both civil and military talent.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Lun was the most famous of the brothers and possessed both civil and military talent.

sentences.zh: 以功臣子少居顯職，位至司會中大夫、開府儀同三司，封河陽郡公。

translations.literal: As the son of a meritorious minister he rose early to prominent office, reaching Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Master of the Office with the same ceremonial rank as the Three Excellencies, and was enfeoffed Duke of Heyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: As the son of a meritorious minister he rose early to high office, eventually reaching Director of the Department of State Affairs with the rank of Grand Master of the Office equal to the Three Excellencies, and was enfeoffed Duke of Heyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 為聘齊使主，卒。

translations.literal: He served as chief envoy on a marriage mission to Qi and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief envoy on a marriage mission to Qi and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子長雅嗣，尚隋文帝女襄國公主，位內史侍郎、河州刺史、檢校秦州總管。

translations.literal: His son Changya succeeded, married Emperor Wen of Sui's daughter the Princess of Xiangguo, and held the posts of Vice Director of the Secretariat, Governor of He Province, and Acting Commander-in-Chief of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changya succeeded him, married Emperor Wen of Sui's daughter, the Princess of Xiangguo, and served as Vice Director of the Secretariat, Governor of He Province, and acting Commander-in-Chief of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 綸弟晏，開府儀同三司、趙郡公，從平齊，歿并州。

translations.literal: Lun's younger brother Yan was a Grand Master of the Office with the same ceremonial rank as the Three Excellencies and Duke of Zhao Commandery; he followed the campaign to pacify Qi and died at Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's younger brother Yan held the rank of Grand Master of the Office equal to the Three Excellencies and the title Duke of Zhao Commandery; he took part in the conquest of Qi and died at Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 子憬，以晏死王事，即襲其官爵。

translations.literal: His son Jing, because Yan died in the king's service, immediately inherited his office and title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing, because Yan had died in the service of the state, immediately inherited his offices and title.

sentences.zh: 曜既不得嗣，朝廷以弼功重，封曜邢國公，位開府。

translations.literal: Since Yao could not inherit, the court, because of Bi's great merit, enfeoffed Yao as Duke of Xing and gave him the rank of Grand Master of the Office.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yao could not inherit the main line, the court, honoring Bi's great service, enfeoffed Yao as Duke of Xing with the rank of Grand Master of the Office.

sentences.zh: 子寬，幹略過人，自周及隋，數經將領，位柱國、蒲山郡公，號為名將。

translations.literal: His son Kuan surpassed others in ability and strategy; from Zhou through Sui he repeatedly commanded armies, reached the rank of Pillar of the State and Duke of Poshan Commandery, and was acclaimed as a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuan surpassed others in ability and strategic insight; from Zhou through Sui he repeatedly held command, rose to Pillar of the State and Duke of Poshan Commandery, and was renowned as a leading general.

sentences.zh: 弼弟摽，字雲傑，長不盈五尺，性果決，有膽氣。

translations.literal: Bi’s younger brother Biao, courtesy name Yunjie, was less than five chi tall, but his nature was decisive and he had courage.
translations.idiomatic: Bi’s younger brother Biao was styled Yunjie. He was under five chi tall, but decisive by nature and full of courage.

sentences.zh: 魏永安元年，以兼別將從爾硃榮破元顥。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yong’an under Wei, as acting detached general, he followed Erzhu Rong in defeating Yuan Hao.
translations.idiomatic: In 528, serving as acting detached general, he followed Erzhu Rong in defeating Yuan Hao.

sentences.zh: 榮誅，隨爾硃兆入洛。

translations.literal: When Rong was executed, he followed Erzhu Zhao into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong was executed, he followed Erzhu Zhao into Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及魏孝武西遷，摽從都督元斌之興齊神武戰，敗，遂與斌之奔梁。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Biao followed the commander Yuan Binzhi in raising troops to fight Qi Shenwu; they were defeated, and he then fled to Liang with Binzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Biao followed the commander Yuan Binzhi in fighting Qi Shenwu. Defeated, he fled to Liang with Binzhi.

sentences.zh: 後得逃發，進封晉陽縣子。

translations.literal: Later he managed to escape, and was advanced in fief to Viscount of Jinyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Later he managed to escape and was promoted to Viscount of Jinyang County.

sentences.zh: 尋為周文帝帳內都督，從復弘農，破沙苑。

translations.literal: Soon he became Commander within Emperor Wen of Zhou’s tent, followed in recovering Hongnong, and broke the enemy at Shayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Commander within Emperor Wen of Zhou’s tent, took part in recovering Hongnong, and helped win the victory at Shayuan.

sentences.zh: 摽時跨馬運矛，沖堅陷隱陣，隱身鞍甲之中。

translations.literal: At the time Bi rode a horse wielding a spear, charged strongpoints and broke hidden formations, and concealed himself amid saddle and armor.
translations.idiomatic: In battle Bi would ride forth wielding a spear, smash through strongpoints and hidden formations, and conceal himself amid saddle and armor.

sentences.zh: 敵人見之，皆曰「避此小兒」。

translations.literal: When enemies saw him, they all said, "Avoid this little fellow."
translations.idiomatic: Enemies who saw him would say, "Keep clear of that little fellow."

sentences.zh: 不知摽之形貌，正自如此。

translations.literal: They did not know that Bi's appearance was exactly like this.
translations.idiomatic: They did not realize that Bi's appearance was exactly as they described.

sentences.zh: 周文初亦聞摽驍悍，未見其能，至是方嗟歎之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou had at first also heard that Bi was fierce and bold but had not yet seen his ability; only then did he sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou had heard that Bi was fierce and bold but had not yet seen him in action; only now did he sigh in admiration.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「但問膽決如何，何必要須八尺之軀也。」

translations.literal: He said to him: "One need only ask how bold and resolute a man is—why must he necessarily stand eight feet tall?"
translations.idiomatic: He told him, "What matters is courage and resolve—why must a warrior stand eight feet tall?"

sentences.zh: 以功進爵為公。

translations.literal: For his merit his title was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements his title was advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 武成初，從豆盧甯征稽胡，進爵汝南郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng he followed Doulu Ning in campaigning against the Ji Hu and was advanced to Duke of Runan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wucheng era he campaigned against the Ji Hu under Doulu Ning and was enfeoffed Duke of Runan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 出為總管延綏丹三州諸軍事、延州刺史，卒官。

translations.literal: He went out as Commander-in-Chief over the military affairs of Yan, Sui, and Dan Provinces and as Governor of Yan Province, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Commander-in-Chief over Yan, Sui, and Dan Provinces and Governor of Yan Province, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 無子，以弼子椿嗣，位開府儀同大將軍、右宮伯，改封河東郡公。

translations.literal: Having no son, Bi's son Chun succeeded him, holding the posts of Grand Master of the Office, General of the Same Rank, and Right Palace Guard and was re-enfeoffed Duke of Hedong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son, so Bi's son Chun succeeded him as Grand Master of the Office, General of the Same Rank, and Right Palace Guard, and was re-enfeoffed Duke of Hedong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 密字法主，蒲山公寬之子也。

translations.literal: Mi, styled Fazhu, was the son of Duke of Poshan Kuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mi, courtesy name Fazhu, was the son of Kuan, Duke of Poshan.

sentences.zh: 才兼文武，志氣雄遠，少襲爵蒲山公。

translations.literal: He combined civil and military talent, his ambition was bold and far-reaching, and from youth he inherited the title Duke of Poshan.
translations.idiomatic: He combined civil and military gifts, his ambitions were bold and far-reaching, and from youth he inherited the title Duke of Poshan.

sentences.zh: 養客禮賢，無所愛吝。

translations.literal: He kept retainers and honored the worthy, sparing nothing in generosity.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a household of retainers and treated men of talent with lavish generosity.

sentences.zh: 與楊玄感為刎頸交。

translations.literal: He was a sworn friend of Yang Xuangan.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yang Xuangan were sworn friends.

sentences.zh: 後更折節耽學，尤好兵書，謂皆在口。

translations.literal: Later he restrained himself and devoted himself to study, especially loving books of war, which he said were all on his lips.
translations.idiomatic: Later he applied himself to study with renewed discipline, especially devouring books of war, which he could recite from memory.

sentences.zh: 師事國子助教包愷，受史記、漢書。

translations.literal: He took as teacher Bao Kai, Assistant Instructor at the Imperial Academy, and studied the Records of the Grand Historian and the Book of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Bao Kai, assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy, and mastered the Records of the Grand Historian and the Book of Han.

sentences.zh: 愷門徒皆出其下。

translations.literal: All of Kai's disciples were beneath him.
translations.idiomatic: He surpassed all of Kai's other pupils.

sentences.zh: 大業初，授親衛大都督，以疾歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was appointed Grand Commander of the Personal Guard, then returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daye era he was appointed Grand Commander of the Personal Guard, but returned home because of illness.

sentences.zh: 及玄感有逆謀，召密，令與弟玄挺赴黎陽，以為謀主。

translations.literal: When Xuangan formed a treasonous plot, he summoned Mi and ordered him and his younger brother Xuanting to go to Liyang as chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuangan plotted rebellion, he summoned Mi and ordered him and his younger brother Xuanting to Liyang to serve as chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 密進三計曰：「今天子遠在遼外，公長驅入薊，直扼其喉，前有高麗，退無歸路，不戰而禽，此計上也。

translations.literal: Mi offered three plans, saying: "Today the Son of Heaven is far away in Liaodong. My lord should drive straight into Ji, seize his throat directly; with Goguryeo ahead and no road of retreat behind, he can be taken without fighting—this is the upper plan.
translations.idiomatic: Mi offered three plans: "The emperor is far away in Liaodong. If you drive straight into Ji and seize his throat, with Goguryeo ahead and no line of retreat behind, he can be captured without a battle. That is the best plan.

sentences.zh: 又關中四塞，衛文升不足為意，今率眾務早入西，萬全之勢，此計中也。

translations.literal: Further, the passes of Guanzhong are secure on four sides, and Wei Wensheng is not worth worrying about; now lead the host and strive to enter the west early—this is the secure plan, the middle plan.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong is protected on four sides, and Wei Wensheng is no serious threat. If you march west at once with your full force, the position will be secure. That is the second plan.

sentences.zh: 若隨近先向東都，以引歲月，此計之下也。」

translations.literal: If you first turn toward the Eastern Capital nearby and draw matters out for months, this is the lower plan."
translations.idiomatic: If you turn first toward the nearby Eastern Capital and drag matters out for months, that is the worst plan."

sentences.zh: 玄感曰：「公下計乃上策矣。

translations.literal: Xuangan said: "Your lower plan is actually the upper strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan said, "Your worst plan is actually the best strategy.

sentences.zh: 今百官家口並在東都，若不取之，安能動物？

translations.literal: Now the families of all officials are in the Eastern Capital; if we do not take it, how can we stir men's hearts?
translations.idiomatic: The families of all the officials are in the Eastern Capital. If we do not take it, how can we move men's hearts?

sentences.zh: 且經城不拔，何以示威？」

translations.literal: Moreover, if we pass a city without taking it, how can we display authority?"
translations.idiomatic: And if we pass a city without capturing it, how can we show our power?"

sentences.zh: 密計不行。

translations.literal: Mi's plan was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's plan was rejected.

sentences.zh: 玄感既至東都，自謂功在朝夕。

translations.literal: Once Xuangan reached the Eastern Capital, he considered success a matter of days.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xuangan reached the Eastern Capital, he thought victory was only days away.

sentences.zh: 及獲韋福嗣，既非同謀，設籌皆持兩端。

translations.literal: When he captured Wei Fusi, who was not a fellow conspirator, every plan he offered was hedged on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: When he captured Wei Fusi, who was not a fellow conspirator, every plan Fusi offered was equivocal.

sentences.zh: 玄感後使作檄文，固辭不肯。

translations.literal: Later Xuangan had him compose a proclamation, but he firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Xuangan ordered him to draft a proclamation, he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 密揣知其情，請斬之。

translations.literal: Mi guessed his intentions and asked that he be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Mi read his intentions and asked that he be executed.

sentences.zh: 玄感不從。

translations.literal: Xuangan did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan refused.

sentences.zh: 密退謂所親曰：「楚公好反而不欲勝，吾屬今為虜矣。」

translations.literal: Mi withdrew and said to those close to him: "The Duke of Chu loves rebellion but does not wish to win; we are captives now."
translations.idiomatic: Mi withdrew and told those close to him, "The Duke of Chu loves rebellion but does not want victory. We are prisoners already."

sentences.zh: 後玄感將西入，福嗣晚亡歸東都。

translations.literal: Later, when Xuangan was about to march west, Fusi escaped by night and returned to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Xuangan was about to march west, Fusi escaped by night and returned to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 時李雄勸玄感速稱尊號，玄感以問密，密以為不可。

translations.literal: At the time Li Xiong urged Xuangan to declare himself emperor at once; Xuangan asked Mi, and Mi thought it inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Xiong urged Xuangan to declare himself emperor at once. Xuangan asked Mi, who thought it unwise.

sentences.zh: 玄感笑而止。

translations.literal: Xuangan laughed and dropped the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan laughed and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 及宇文述、來護等軍且至，玄感謂密計將安出。

translations.literal: When the armies of Yuwen Shu, Lai Hu, and others were about to arrive, Xuangan asked Mi what plan he would offer.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies of Yuwen Shu, Lai Hu, and others were about to arrive, Xuangan asked Mi what plan he had.

sentences.zh: 密曰：「元弘嗣統強兵於隴右，今可揚言其反，遣使迎公，因此入關，可得紿眾。」

translations.literal: Mi said: "Yuan Hongsi commands strong troops in Longyou; now we can spread word that he has rebelled and send envoys to welcome you, and by this means enter the passes and deceive the host."
translations.idiomatic: Mi said, "Yuan Hongsi commands strong troops in Longyou. We can spread word that he has rebelled and send envoys to welcome you. That way we can enter the passes and deceive the army."

sentences.zh: 玄感遂用密謀號令。

translations.literal: Xuangan thereupon adopted Mi's stratagem and issued the orders.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan then adopted Mi's plan and issued the orders accordingly.

sentences.zh: 西至陝縣，圍弘農不拔，西至閿鄉，追兵至，玄感敗。

translations.literal: He marched west to Shan County, besieged Hongnong without taking it, then went west to Wenxiang; pursuing troops arrived and Xuangan was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He marched west to Shan County and besieged Hongnong without success, then continued west to Wenxiang; pursuing troops caught up and Xuangan was defeated.

sentences.zh: 密間行入關，與玄感從叔詢相隨，匿馮翊詢妻家。

translations.literal: Mi entered the passes by secret routes, followed by Xuangan's cousin Xun, and hid at Xun's wife's family home in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Mi slipped into the passes by secret routes with Xuangan's cousin Xun and hid at Xun's wife's family home in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 尋為鄰人告，被捕，與其黨俱送帝所。

translations.literal: Soon he was reported by a neighbor, arrested, and sent with his followers to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a neighbor reported them; Mi was arrested and sent with his followers to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 在途，與其眾謀逃。

translations.literal: On the road he plotted escape with his men.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he plotted escape with his companions.

sentences.zh: 其徒多金，密令出示使者曰：「吾等死日，此金留付公，幸用相瘞，其餘即皆報德。」

translations.literal: His followers had much gold; Mi had it shown to the escort and said: "On the day we die, this gold is left to you, sir—please use it for our burial; the rest will repay your kindness."
translations.idiomatic: His companions had a good deal of gold. Mi showed it to the escort and said, "When we die, this gold is yours—please use it to bury us properly, and keep the rest as your reward."

sentences.zh: 使者利金，遂相許。

translations.literal: The escort coveted the gold and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The escort, tempted by the gold, agreed.

sentences.zh: 及出關，密每夜宴飲。

translations.literal: After leaving the passes, Mi feasted and drank every night.
translations.idiomatic: After they left the passes, Mi held feasts and drank every night.

sentences.zh: 行次邯鄲，夜宿村中，密等七人皆穿牆而遁。

translations.literal: When they reached Handan and lodged in a village by night, Mi and six others all escaped through holes in the wall.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Handan and lodged in a village one night, Mi and six others escaped through holes in the wall.

sentences.zh: 與王仲伯亡抵平原賊帥郝孝德，孝德不甚禮之。

translations.literal: With Wang Zhongbo he fled to the bandit chief Hao Xiaode of Pingyuan; Xiaode did not treat them with much respect.
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Zhongbo he fled to the bandit leader Hao Xiaode of Pingyuan, who did not treat them well.

sentences.zh: 備遭饑饉，削樹皮而食之。

translations.literal: They suffered famine and ate by stripping tree bark.
translations.idiomatic: They endured famine and survived by stripping bark from trees to eat.

sentences.zh: 仲伯潛歸天水。

translations.literal: Zhongbo secretly returned to Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongbo secretly made his way back to Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 密詣淮陽，舍於村中，變姓名稱劉智遠，聚徒教授。

translations.literal: Mi went to Huaiyang, lodged in a village, changed his name to Liu Zhiyuan, gathered pupils, and taught.
translations.idiomatic: Mi went to Huaiyang, lodged in a village under the name Liu Zhiyuan, gathered pupils, and taught.

sentences.zh: 經數月，鬱鬱不得志，為五言詩，詩成，泣下數行。

translations.literal: After several months, depressed and unfulfilled, he composed a five-character poem; when it was finished, tears streamed down his face.
translations.idiomatic: After several months of frustration he composed a five-character poem; when he finished it, tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 時人有怪之，以告太守趙他，下縣捕之。

translations.literal: Someone found this strange and reported it to Governor Zhao Ta, who ordered the county to arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: Someone found this odd and reported it to Governor Zhao Ta, who ordered the county magistrate to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 密亡抵其妹夫雍丘令丘君明。

translations.literal: Mi fled to his brother-in-law Qiu Junming, Magistrate of Yongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Mi fled to his brother-in-law Qiu Junming, magistrate of Yongqiu.

sentences.zh: 君明從子懷義後告之，密得遁去，君明竟坐死。

translations.literal: Later Junming's nephew Huaiyi reported them; Mi escaped, but Junming was ultimately executed for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Later Junming's nephew Huaiyi reported them. Mi escaped, but Junming was executed for harboring him.

sentences.zh: 密投東郡賊帥翟讓，乃因王伯當以策幹讓。

translations.literal: Mi went to Zhai Rang, bandit chief of Dong Commandery, and through Wang Bodang presented plans to win Rang over.
translations.idiomatic: Mi joined Zhai Rang, the bandit leader of Dong Commandery, and through Wang Bodang offered strategies to win him over.

sentences.zh: 遣說諸小賊，所至輒降，讓始敬焉，召與計事。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to persuade the lesser bandits, and wherever they went they submitted; Rang then began to respect him and summoned him to counsel on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to win over lesser bandit bands, and wherever they went the bands surrendered. Rang then began to respect him and summoned him to discuss strategy.

sentences.zh: 密以兵眾無糧，勸讓直趣滎陽，休兵館穀，然後爭利。

translations.literal: Mi, because the army had no grain, urged Rang to march straight to Xingyang, rest the troops and store grain, and then contend for advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Because the army lacked provisions, Mi urged Rang to march straight to Xingyang, rest the troops, stockpile grain, and then fight for advantage.

sentences.zh: 讓從之，乃掠下滎陽。

translations.literal: Rang agreed and thereupon raided down into Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Rang agreed and raided south into Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 太守郇王慶及通守張須陀以兵討讓。

translations.literal: Governor Xing Wang Qing and Assistant Governor Zhang Xutuo led troops to attack Rang.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Xing Wang Qing and Assistant Governor Zhang Xutuo marched against Rang with government troops.

sentences.zh: 讓數為須陀敗，將遠避之。

translations.literal: Rang was repeatedly defeated by Xutuo and was about to flee far away to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: Rang was repeatedly defeated by Xutuo and prepared to flee far away.

sentences.zh: 密勸讓列陣以待，密以奇兵掩擊，大破之，斬須陀於陣。

translations.literal: Mi urged Rang to draw up battle lines and wait; Mi then struck with surprise troops and routed the enemy, beheading Xutuo on the field.
translations.idiomatic: Mi urged Rang to form battle lines and wait; then Mi struck with a flanking force, routed the enemy, and killed Xutuo in battle.

sentences.zh: 讓於是令密建牙，別統所部。

translations.literal: Rang thereupon had Mi raise his own command banner and separately command his own forces.
translations.idiomatic: Rang then allowed Mi to raise his own command banner and lead his own troops independently.

sentences.zh: 復說讓以廓清天下為事，令掩據興洛倉，發粟以振窮乏。

translations.literal: He again urged Rang to make pacifying the realm his task, seize Xingluo Granary by surprise, and distribute grain to relieve the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: He again urged Rang to set his sights on pacifying the realm, seize Xingluo Granary by surprise, and distribute grain to relieve the poor.

sentences.zh: 於是興讓以義甯元年春出陽城，北逾方山，自羅口襲興洛倉，破之，開倉振百姓。

translations.literal: Thereupon Rang in the spring of the first year of Yining marched out from Yangcheng, crossed Fang Mountain to the north, struck Xingluo Granary from Luokou, took it, opened the granary, and relieved the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Yining, Rang marched out from Yangcheng, crossed Fang Mountain to the north, struck Xingluo Granary from Luokou, captured it, opened the stores, and fed the people.

sentences.zh: 越王侗遣武賁郎將劉長恭討密。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Tong sent Martial Guard General Liu Changgong to attack Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yue Yang Tong sent Martial Guard General Liu Changgong to attack Mi.

sentences.zh: 密一戰破之，長恭僅以身免。

translations.literal: Mi defeated him in a single battle; Changgong barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Mi routed him in a single battle; Changgong barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 讓於是推密為主。

translations.literal: Rang thereupon made Mi leader.
translations.idiomatic: Rang then acknowledged Mi as leader.

sentences.zh: 密城洛口周回四十城以居之。

translations.literal: Mi fortified Luokou, forty li in circumference, and made it his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Mi fortified Luokou, a settlement forty li in circumference, and made it his base.

sentences.zh: 讓上密號為魏公，設壇場即位，稱元年。

translations.literal: Rang gave Mi the title Duke of Wei, set up an altar for his enthronement, and proclaimed the first year of his reign.
translations.idiomatic: Rang gave Mi the title Duke of Wei; Mi set up an altar, took office, and proclaimed the first year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 以房彥藻為左長史，邴元真為右長史，楊德方為左司馬，鄭德韜為右司馬。

translations.literal: He appointed Fang Yanzao Left Chief Clerk, Bing Yuanzhen Right Chief Clerk, Yang Defang Left Major, and Zheng Detao Right Major.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Fang Yanzao Left Chief Clerk, Bing Yuanzhen Right Chief Clerk, Yang Defang Left Major, and Zheng Detao Right Major.

sentences.zh: 拜讓為司徒，封東郡公。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Rang as Minister over the Masses and Duke of Dong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He made Rang Minister over the Masses and enfeoffed him Duke of Dong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 長白山賊孟讓掠東郡，燒豐都市而歸。

translations.literal: Meng Rang, a bandit of Mount Changbai, raided Dong Commandery, burned Fengdu Market, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Rang, a bandit leader from Mount Changbai, raided Dong Commandery, burned Fengdu Market, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 密攻下鞏縣，獲縣長柴孝和，拜為護軍。

translations.literal: Mi captured Gong County, took its magistrate Chai Xiaohe, and appointed him Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Mi captured Gong County, took its magistrate Chai Xiaohe prisoner, and made him Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 武賁郎將裴仁基以武牢歸密，密因遣仁基與孟讓襲破回洛倉，據之。

translations.literal: Martial Guard General Pei Renji surrendered Wulao to Mi; Mi then sent Renji with Meng Rang to strike and take Huiluo Granary and hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Martial Guard General Pei Renji surrendered Wulao to Mi; Mi then sent Renji with Meng Rang to seize Huiluo Granary, which they captured and held.

sentences.zh: 俄而德韜、德方俱死，筆以鄭頲為左司馬，鄭虔象為右司馬。

translations.literal: Soon Detao and Defang both died; he then appointed Zheng Ting Left Major and Zheng Qianxiang Right Major.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Detao and Defang both died; Mi then appointed Zheng Ting Left Major and Zheng Qianxiang Right Major.

sentences.zh: 柴孝和說密令裴仁基守回洛，翟讓據洛口，身率精銳，西襲長安，不然他人我先。

translations.literal: Chai Xiaohe urged Mi to have Pei Renji hold Huiluo, Zhai Rang hold Luokou, and himself lead elite troops west to strike Chang'an, or else others would get there first.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Xiaohe urged Mi to leave Pei Renji to hold Huiluo, Zhai Rang to hold Luokou, and himself to lead elite troops west against Chang'an—otherwise someone else would get there first.

sentences.zh: 密曰：「此誠上策，然我之所部並山東人，既見未下洛陽，恐不肯西入。」

translations.literal: Mi said: "This is indeed the upper plan, but my followers are all men of Shandong; seeing that Luoyang has not yet fallen, I fear they will not agree to march west."
translations.idiomatic: Mi said, "That is indeed the best plan, but my followers are all men from the east. Seeing that Luoyang has not yet fallen, I fear they will refuse to march west."

sentences.zh: 孝和請間行觀隙，乃與數十騎至陝縣，賊歸之者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Xiaohe asked to go by secret routes and watch for openings; he then went with several dozen horsemen to Shan County, and more than ten thousand bandits joined him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaohe asked to travel by secret routes and watch for an opening; he went with several dozen horsemen to Shan County, and more than ten thousand rebels joined him.

sentences.zh: 密時兵鋒甚銳，每入苑與官軍連戰。

translations.literal: At the time Mi's army was very sharp; whenever it entered the park it fought continuously with government troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Mi's army was at its peak; whenever it entered the imperial park it fought continuously with government troops.

sentences.zh: 會密為流矢所中，臥于營內，東都出兵擊之，密眾大潰，棄回洛倉歸洛口。

translations.literal: When Mi was struck by a stray arrow and lay ill in camp, the Eastern Capital sent troops to attack; Mi's host was routed, abandoned Huiluo Granary, and returned to Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi was struck by a stray arrow and lay wounded in camp, the Eastern Capital sent troops against him; his army was routed, abandoned Huiluo Granary, and retreated to Luokou.

sentences.zh: 孝和之眾聞密敗，各分散而去，孝和輕騎歸密。

translations.literal: When Xiaohe's men heard that Mi had been defeated, they scattered and left; Xiaohe returned to Mi with a small escort.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaohe's followers heard of Mi's defeat, they scattered; Xiaohe returned to Mi with a small escort.

sentences.zh: 煬帝遣王世充率江淮勁卒五萬討密，敗之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang sent Wang Shichong with fifty thousand elite troops from the Jianghuai region to attack Mi and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang sent Wang Shichong with fifty thousand elite troops from the Jianghuai region against Mi and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 孝和溺洛水，密甚傷之。

translations.literal: Xiaohe drowned in the Luo River; Mi grieved deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaohe drowned in the Luo River, and Mi grieved deeply.

sentences.zh: 世充營於洛西，與密相拒百餘日。

translations.literal: Shichong encamped west of the Luo and faced Mi for more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong encamped west of the Luo and remained locked in stalemate with Mi for more than a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 武陽郡丞元寶藏、黎陽賊帥李文相、洹水賊帥張升、清河賊帥趙君德、平原賊帥郝孝德並歸密，共襲破黎陽倉，據之。

translations.literal: Assistant Administrator of Wuyang Yuan Baocang, bandit chief of Liyang Li Wenxiang, bandit chief of Huanshui Zhang Sheng, bandit chief of Qinghe Zhao Junde, and bandit chief of Pingyuan Hao Xiaode all submitted to Mi; together they struck and took Liyang Granary and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Baocang, assistant administrator of Wuyang; Li Wenxiang, bandit leader of Liyang; Zhang Sheng, bandit leader of Huanshui; Zhao Junde, bandit leader of Qinghe; and Hao Xiaode, bandit leader of Pingyuan—all submitted to Mi, joined in seizing Liyang Granary, and held it.

sentences.zh: 周法明舉江、黃之地以附密。

translations.literal: Zhou Faming raised the lands of the Jiang and Huang regions in submission to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Faming brought the lands along the Yangtze and Han rivers over to Mi's side.

sentences.zh: 齊郡賊帥徐圓朗、任城大俠徐師仁、淮陽太守趙他等前後款附以千百數。

translations.literal: Bandit chief of Qi Commandery Xu Yuanlang, chivalrous hero of Rencheng Xu Shiren, Governor of Huaiyang Zhao Ta, and others successively submitted in numbers of hundreds and thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanlang, bandit leader of Qi Commandery; Xu Shiren, a chivalrous hero of Rencheng; Zhao Ta, governor of Huaiyang; and others submitted in succession, numbering in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 翟讓所部王儒信勸讓為太宰，總眾務以奪密權。

translations.literal: Wang Ruxin of Zhai Rang's command urged Rang to become Grand Minister and control all affairs to seize Mi's power.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ruxin, one of Zhai Rang's officers, urged Rang to become Grand Minister, take control of all affairs, and seize power from Mi.

sentences.zh: 兄寬復謂讓曰：「天子止可自作，安得與人？

translations.literal: His elder brother Kuan again said to Rang: "The Son of Heaven can only be made by oneself—how can one share it with another?
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Kuan again told Rang, "A man makes himself emperor—how can he share that role with another?

sentences.zh: 汝若不作，我當為之。」

translations.literal: If you will not do it, I shall."
translations.idiomatic: If you will not do it, I will."

sentences.zh: 密聞，惡之。

translations.literal: When Mi heard this, he hated it.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi heard of this, he was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 會讓拒世充，軍退數百步，密與單雄信等赴之，世充敗走。

translations.literal: When Rang was resisting Shichong and his army had retreated several hundred paces, Mi with Shan Xiongxin and others rushed to help; Shichong was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Rang was holding off Shichong and his line had fallen back several hundred paces, Mi rushed to his aid with Shan Xiongxin and others; Shichong was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 讓欲乘勝破其營，會日暮，固止之。

translations.literal: Rang wished to follow up the victory and destroy Shichong's camp, but as night fell Mi firmly stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Rang wanted to press the victory and destroy Shichong's camp, but night fell and Mi firmly stopped him.

sentences.zh: 明日，讓與數百人至密所，欲為宴樂。

translations.literal: The next day Rang came with several hundred men to Mi's quarters intending to feast and make merry.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Rang came to Mi's quarters with several hundred men for a feast.

sentences.zh: 其所將左右各就食，諸門並設備，讓不覺。

translations.literal: The attendants he brought each went to eat; at every gate preparations were made, but Rang did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants Rang brought each went off to eat; at every gate Mi's men stood ready, but Rang noticed nothing.

sentences.zh: 密引讓入坐，令讓射。

translations.literal: Mi led Rang in to sit and had Rang shoot.
translations.idiomatic: Mi invited Rang to sit and asked him to shoot.

sentences.zh: 引滿將發，密遣壯士蔡建自後斬之。

translations.literal: As he drew the bow full and was about to release, Mi sent the strongman Cai Jian to cut him down from behind.
translations.idiomatic: As Rang drew the bow full and was about to release, Mi had the strongman Cai Jian cut him down from behind.

sentences.zh: 遂殺其兄寬及儒信等，從者亦有死焉。

translations.literal: He then killed Rang's elder brother Kuan and Ruxin and others; some of those who accompanied Rang also died.
translations.idiomatic: He then killed Rang's elder brother Kuan, Ruxin, and others; some of Rang's attendants were killed as well.

sentences.zh: 讓部將徐世勳為亂兵所斫，中重創，密止之，僅得免。

translations.literal: Rang's officer Xu Shiji was cut down by the tumultuous soldiers and suffered grave wounds; Mi stopped them, and Shiji barely escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Rang's officer Xu Shiji was struck down in the melee and badly wounded; Mi stopped the attack, and Shiji barely survived.

sentences.zh: 雄信等皆叩頭求哀，密並釋而慰之。

translations.literal: Xiongxin and the others all kowtowed and begged for mercy; Mi released and comforted them all.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongxin and the others all kowtowed and begged for mercy; Mi released them and offered reassurance.

sentences.zh: 於是詣讓營，遣王伯當、邴元真、單雄信等告以殺讓意，令世勳、雄信、伯當分統其眾。

translations.literal: He then went to Rang's camp and sent Wang Bodang, Bing Yuanzhen, Shan Xiongxin, and others to explain why Rang had been killed, and had Shiji, Xiongxin, and Bodang each command part of Rang's forces.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Rang's camp and sent Wang Bodang, Bing Yuanzhen, and Shan Xiongxin to explain why Rang had been killed; he had Shiji, Xiongxin, and Bodang each take command of part of Rang's forces.

sentences.zh: 世充夜襲倉城，密拒破之，斬武賁郎將費青奴。

translations.literal: Shichong raided the granary city by night; Mi repulsed and defeated him and beheaded Martial Guard General Fei Qingnu.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong raided the granary city by night; Mi repulsed him, won the battle, and killed Martial Guard General Fei Qingnu.

sentences.zh: 世充復營洛北，于洛水構浮橋，悉眾擊密。

translations.literal: Shichong again encamped north of the Luo, built a pontoon bridge over the Luo River, and attacked Mi with his entire force.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong encamped again north of the Luo, built a pontoon bridge across the river, and attacked Mi with his full army.

sentences.zh: 密拒之，不利而退。

translations.literal: Mi resisted but fared poorly and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Mi resisted but fared poorly and fell back.

sentences.zh: 世充因薄其城下，密擊之，大潰，爭橋，橋陷，溺水者數萬人。

translations.literal: Shichong pressed close beneath the walls; Mi struck back and routed him; men scrambled for the bridge, the bridge collapsed, and tens of thousands drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong pressed close to the walls; Mi counterattacked and routed him. Men scrambled for the bridge, the bridge collapsed, and tens of thousands drowned.

sentences.zh: 武郎將楊威、王辨、霍世舉、劉長恭梁德重、董智通等皆沒於陣。

translations.literal: Martial Generals Yang Wei, Wang Bian, Huo Shiju, Liu Changgong, Liang Dezhong, Dong Zhitong, and others all perished on the field.
translations.idiomatic: Martial Generals Yang Wei, Wang Bian, Huo Shiju, Liu Changgong, Liang Dezhong, Dong Zhitong, and others were killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 世充僅而獲免，不敢還東都，遂走河陽。

translations.literal: Shichong barely escaped; he dared not return to the Eastern Capital and fled to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong barely escaped with his life, dared not return to the Eastern Capital, and fled to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 其夜大雪，餘眾死亡殆盡。

translations.literal: That night heavy snow fell, and nearly all the remaining troops died.
translations.idiomatic: That night heavy snow fell, and nearly all of Shichong's remaining troops perished.

sentences.zh: 密乃修金墉故城居之，眾三十餘萬，攻上春門。

translations.literal: Mi then restored the old city of Jinyong and made it his residence; his host numbered more than three hundred thousand, and he attacked the Shangchun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Mi restored the old city of Jinyong and made it his base; his forces numbered more than three hundred thousand, and he attacked the Shangchun Gate.

sentences.zh: 留守韋津出戰，被執。

translations.literal: The garrison commander Wei Jin went out to fight and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander Wei Jin went out to fight and was captured.

sentences.zh: 其黨勸密即尊號，密不許。

translations.literal: His followers urged Mi to assume the imperial title at once; Mi refused.
translations.idiomatic: His followers urged Mi to declare himself emperor at once; Mi refused.

sentences.zh: 及義師圍東都，密出軍爭之，交綏而退。

translations.literal: When the righteous armies besieged the Eastern Capital, Mi marched out to contest it, clashed briefly, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous armies besieged the Eastern Capital, Mi marched out to contest the city, clashed briefly, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 俄而宇文化及弑逆，自江都北指黎陽，密拒之。

translations.literal: Soon Yuwen Huaji committed regicide and marched north from Jiangdu toward Liyang; Mi resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor and marched north from Jiangdu toward Liyang; Mi blocked his advance.

sentences.zh: 會越王侗稱尊號，遣使授密太尉、尚書令、東南道大行台、行軍元帥、魏國公，令先平化及，然後入朝輔政。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yue Tong assumed the imperial title, he sent envoys to appoint Mi Grand Commandant, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Commissioner of the Southeast Circuit, Campaign Marshal, and Duke of Wei, ordering him first to pacify Huaji and then enter court to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Yue Yang Tong assumed the imperial title, he sent envoys appointing Mi Grand Commandant, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Commissioner of the Southeast Circuit, Campaign Marshal, and Duke of Wei, with orders to pacify Huaji first and then enter court to assist in government.

sentences.zh: 化及至黎陽，徐世勳守倉城不下。

translations.literal: When Huaji reached Liyang, Xu Shiji held the granary city and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji reached Liyang, Xu Shiji held the granary city and refused to surrender.

sentences.zh: 密共化及隔水語，密數之曰：「卿本匈奴阜隸破野頭耳，父與兄弟皆受隋恩，豈容躬行殺虐？

translations.literal: Mi spoke with Huaji across the water; Mi rebuked him, saying: "You are originally a slave of the Xiongnu, a Poyetou by birth; your father and brothers all received Sui grace—how can you personally commit slaughter and cruelty?
translations.idiomatic: Mi spoke with Huaji across the water and rebuked him: "You are nothing but a Xiongnu slave, a Poyetou by birth. Your father and brothers all received favor from Sui—how can you personally commit murder and cruelty?

sentences.zh: 今若速來歸義，尚可全後嗣。」

translations.literal: If you now come quickly to submit in righteousness, your descendants may still be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: If you submit now, your descendants may still be spared."

sentences.zh: 化及默然，俯仰良久，乃嗔目大言曰：「共你論相殺事，何須作書傳雅語！」

translations.literal: Huaji was silent; after a long while he glared and shouted: "When I discuss killing with you, why must you speak in the elegant language of books and histories!"
translations.idiomatic: Huaji fell silent. After a long pause he glared and shouted, "When we talk about killing each other, why speak in the elegant language of books and histories!"

sentences.zh: 密謂從者曰：「化及庸懦如此，忽欲圖帝王，吾當折杖驅之。」

translations.literal: Mi said to those with him: "Huaji is so mediocre and cowardly, yet he suddenly wants to become emperor—I shall drive him off with a broken staff."
translations.idiomatic: Mi told those with him, "Huaji is this mediocre and cowardly, yet he suddenly wants to become emperor. I shall drive him off with a broken staff."

sentences.zh: 知其糧且盡，在偽與之和。

translations.literal: Knowing that Huaji's grain was nearly exhausted, he falsely made peace with him.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Huaji's supplies were nearly exhausted, he feigned a truce.

sentences.zh: 化及大喜，恣其兵食，冀密饋之。

translations.literal: Huaji was greatly pleased, let his troops eat freely, and hoped Mi would supply him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji was delighted, let his troops eat freely, and hoped Mi would feed him.

sentences.zh: 會密下有人獲罪，亡投之，具言密情。

translations.literal: When a man under Mi who had been punished fled to Huaji and fully explained Mi's intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Then a man under Mi who had been punished fled to Huaji and revealed Mi's entire plan.

sentences.zh: 化及大怒，又食盡，與密戰於童山下。

translations.literal: Huaji was furious; his food was also exhausted, and he fought Mi at Mount Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji was furious; his supplies were also exhausted, and he fought Mi at Mount Tong.

sentences.zh: 自辰達酉，密中流矢，頓於汲縣。

translations.literal: From the hour of chen until the hour of you they fought; Mi was struck by a stray arrow and halted at Ji County.
translations.idiomatic: They fought from morning until evening; Mi was struck by a stray arrow and halted at Ji County.

sentences.zh: 化及掠汲郡，北趣魏縣，以輜重留於東郡，遣其刑部尚書王軌守之。

translations.literal: Huaji plundered Ji Commandery and marched north toward Wei County, leaving baggage at Dong Commandery and sending his Minister of Justice Wang Gui to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji plundered Ji Commandery and marched north toward Wei County, leaving his baggage train at Dong Commandery under the guard of his Minister of Justice Wang Gui.

sentences.zh: 軌以郡降，密以軌為滑州總管。

translations.literal: Gui surrendered the commandery; Mi made Gui Commander-in-Chief of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: Gui surrendered the commandery, and Mi appointed him Commander-in-Chief of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 密引兵而西，遣記室參軍李儉朝於東都，執弑帝人于弘達以獻越王侗。

translations.literal: Mi led his troops west and sent Staff Officer Li Jian to court at the Eastern Capital, capturing Yu Hongda, who had murdered the emperor, and presenting him to Prince of Yue Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Mi marched west and sent Staff Officer Li Jian to court at the Eastern Capital with Yu Hongda, one of the emperor's murderers, as a captive for Prince of Yue Yang Tong.

sentences.zh: 侗以儉為司農少卿，使召密入朝。

translations.literal: Tong made Jian Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture and sent him to summon Mi to court.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tong made Jian Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture and sent him to summon Mi to court.

sentences.zh: 密至溫縣，聞世充已殺元文都、盧楚等，乃歸金墉城。

translations.literal: When Mi reached Wen County he heard that Shichong had already killed Yuan Wendu, Lu Chu, and others, and returned to Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi reached Wen County he learned that Shichong had already killed Yuan Wendu, Lu Chu, and others, and returned to Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 世充既擅要權，乃厚賜將士。

translations.literal: Shichong, having seized key power, then lavished rewards on officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong, having seized real power, lavished rewards on his officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 時密兵少衣，世充乏食，乃請交易。

translations.literal: At the time Mi's army lacked clothing and Shichong lacked food, so they requested to trade.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's army lacked clothing and Shichong lacked food, so they proposed to trade.

sentences.zh: 邴元真等各求私利，遽勸密，密許焉。

translations.literal: Bing Yuanzhen and the others each sought private profit and urgently urged Mi; Mi agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuanzhen and the others, each seeking private profit, urgently urged Mi to agree, and Mi consented.

sentences.zh: 初東都絕糧，人歸密者日有數百，至此得食，降人益少。

translations.literal: At first the Eastern Capital had no grain, and hundreds of people submitted to Mi each day; once they obtained food there, fewer and fewer came over.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Eastern Capital had no grain, and hundreds of people defected to Mi each day; once they could obtain food there, fewer and fewer came over.

sentences.zh: 密悔而止。

translations.literal: Mi regretted it and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Mi regretted the decision and halted the trade.

sentences.zh: 密雖據倉，無府庫，兵數戰不賞，又厚撫初附兵，於是眾心漸怨。

translations.literal: Although Mi held the granary, he had no treasury; his troops fought repeatedly without reward, yet he treated newly submitted soldiers generously, and so hearts gradually turned resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Although Mi held the granaries, he had no treasury; his troops fought repeatedly without reward while he treated newly submitted soldiers generously, and discontent spread.

sentences.zh: 時邴元真守洛口倉，性貪鄙。

translations.literal: At the time Bing Yuanzhen guarded Luokou Granary and was greedy and base by nature.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Bing Yuanzhen guarded Luokou Granary and was greedy and corrupt by nature.

sentences.zh: 宇文溫每謂密曰：「不殺元真，公難未已。」

translations.literal: Yuwen Wen often said to Mi: "If Yuanzhen is not killed, your troubles will not end."
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Wen often told Mi, "If Yuanzhen is not killed, your troubles will not end."

sentences.zh: 密不答。

translations.literal: Mi did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Mi did not answer.

sentences.zh: 而元真知之，謀叛。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen learned of this and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen learned of this and plotted to defect.

sentences.zh: 楊慶聞而告密，密因疑焉。

translations.literal: Yang Qing heard of it and reported to Mi; Mi therefore grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qing heard of it and reported to Mi, who grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 會世充悉眾來戰，密留王伯當守金墉，自就偃師，北阻芒山以待之。

translations.literal: When Shichong came with his entire force to fight, Mi left Wang Bodang to guard Jinyong and himself went to Yanshi, blocking Mang Mountain to the north to await him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong marched against him with his full army, Mi left Wang Bodang to guard Jinyong and went to Yanshi, taking position north of Mang Mountain to await him.

sentences.zh: 世充令數百騎度御河，密遣裴行儼等逆之。

translations.literal: Shichong sent several hundred horsemen across the Yu River; Mi dispatched Pei Xingyan and others to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong sent several hundred horsemen across the Yu River; Mi sent Pei Xingyan and others to intercept them.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，行儼、孫長樂、程咬金等驍將十數人皆重創，密甚惡之。

translations.literal: As night fell, Xingyan, Sun Changle, Cheng Yaojin, and more than ten other fierce generals were all badly wounded; Mi was greatly dismayed.
translations.idiomatic: By nightfall Xingyan, Sun Changle, Cheng Yaojin, and more than ten other fierce generals had all been badly wounded; Mi was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 世充夜潛，詰朝而陣，密方覺之。

translations.literal: Shichong moved by night in secret; by the next morning his battle lines were formed before Mi noticed.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong moved by night in secret; by dawn his battle lines were formed before Mi realized what was happening.

sentences.zh: 狼狽出戰，敗績，馳向洛口。

translations.literal: In disarray he went out to fight, was defeated, and galloped toward Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: Mi rushed out to fight in disarray, was defeated, and galloped toward Luokou.

sentences.zh: 世充夜圍偃師，守將鄭頲為其部下，翻城而降世充。

translations.literal: Shichong besieged Yanshi by night; the garrison commander Zheng Ting was turned by his subordinates, who opened the city and surrendered to Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong besieged Yanshi by night; garrison commander Zheng Ting was betrayed by his subordinates, who opened the city and surrendered to Shichong.

sentences.zh: 密將入洛口倉城，元真已遣人引世充。

translations.literal: As Mi was about to enter Luokou Granary city, Yuanzhen had already sent men to guide Shichong in.
translations.idiomatic: As Mi was about to enter Luokou Granary city, Yuanzhen had already sent men to guide Shichong in.

sentences.zh: 密陰知之，不發其事，欲待世充兵半度洛水，然後擊之。

translations.literal: Mi secretly knew this but did not reveal it, intending to wait until half of Shichong's troops had crossed the Luo and then strike.
translations.idiomatic: Mi secretly knew this but said nothing, intending to wait until half of Shichong's army had crossed the Luo and then attack.

sentences.zh: 密候騎不時覺，比將出戰，世充軍悉已濟。

translations.literal: Mi's scouts did not notice in time; by the time he was about to go out to fight, Shichong's entire army had already crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's scouts failed to notice in time; by the time he prepared to attack, Shichong's entire army had already crossed.

sentences.zh: 密引騎而遁，元真以城降世充。

translations.literal: Mi fled with his horsemen; Yuanzhen surrendered the city to Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Mi fled with his cavalry; Yuanzhen surrendered the city to Shichong.

sentences.zh: 密眾漸離，將如黎陽。

translations.literal: Mi's followers gradually departed; he was about to go to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's followers gradually deserted him; he prepared to go to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 人或曰：「殺翟讓之際，徐世勳幾死，其心安可保？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "When Zhai Rang was killed, Xu Shiji nearly died—how can his loyalty be trusted?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "When Zhai Rang was killed, Xu Shiji nearly died himself—how can his loyalty be trusted?"

sentences.zh: 密乃止。

translations.literal: Mi thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Mi then abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 時王伯當棄金墉城，保河陽，密自武牢濟，歸之。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Bodang had abandoned Jinyong and held Heyang; Mi crossed from Wulao and joined him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bodang had abandoned Jinyong and held Heyang; Mi crossed from Wulao and joined him.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「久苦諸君，我今日自刎以謝眾。」

translations.literal: He said: "I have long troubled you all; today I shall cut my own throat to apologize to the host."
translations.idiomatic: He told them, "I have long burdened you all; today I shall take my own life to make amends."

sentences.zh: 眾皆泣，莫能仰視。

translations.literal: All wept and none could look up at him.
translations.idiomatic: All wept, and none could bear to look at him.

sentences.zh: 密復曰：「諸君幸不相棄，當共歸關中。

translations.literal: Mi again said: "If you are willing not to abandon me, we should return together to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Mi then said, "If you are willing to stay with me, we shall return together to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 密身雖愧無功，諸君必保富貴。」

translations.literal: Although I am ashamed to have achieved nothing, you all will surely preserve wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: Though I have achieved nothing and am ashamed, you will all surely preserve your wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 其府掾柳燮曰：「明公與長安宗族，有疇昔之遇，雖不陪起義，然阻東都，斷隋歸路，使唐國不戰而得京師，此公之功也。」

translations.literal: His staff officer Liu Xie said: "My lord and the clans of Chang'an have an old connection; although you did not join the uprising, you blocked the Eastern Capital and cut off Sui's line of retreat, enabling the Tang state to take the capital without fighting—this is your merit."
translations.idiomatic: His staff officer Liu Xie said, "My lord and the clans of Chang'an have long-standing ties. Though you did not join the uprising, you blocked the Eastern Capital and cut off Sui's retreat, allowing the Tang to take the capital without a battle. That is your achievement."

sentences.zh: 眾咸曰：「然。」

translations.literal: All said: "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: All said, "It is so."

sentences.zh: 密遂歸朝，封邢國公，拜光祿卿。

translations.literal: Mi thereupon submitted to the court, was enfeoffed Duke of Xing, and appointed Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: Mi then submitted to the court, was enfeoffed Duke of Xing, and appointed Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 尋奉使出關安撫，至熊州而逃叛，見殺。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent on mission beyond the passes to pacify the region; when he reached Xiong Province he fled in rebellion and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent beyond the passes on a pacification mission; when he reached Xiong Province he rebelled and fled, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 宇文貴，字永貴，其先昌黎大棘人也，徙居夏州。

translations.literal: Yuwen Gui, styled Yonggui, was originally from Daji in Changli; his family moved to Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Gui, courtesy name Yonggui, came from a family originally of Daji in Changli that had moved to Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 父莫豆幹，保定中，以貴勳追贈柱國大將軍、少傅、夏州刺史、安平郡公。

translations.literal: His father Modougan, during Baoding, was posthumously made Pillar of the State, Grand General, Junior Tutor, Governor of Xia Province, and Duke of Anping Commandery for Gui's merit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Modougan was posthumously enfeoffed Pillar of the State, Grand General, Junior Tutor, Governor of Xia Province, and Duke of Anping Commandery during Baoding for Gui's achievements.

sentences.zh: 貴母初孕貴，夢老人抱一子授之曰：「賜爾是子，俾壽且貴。」

translations.literal: When Gui's mother first carried him, she dreamed an old man holding a child gave him to her, saying: "I grant you this child, that he may live long and attain nobility."
translations.idiomatic: When Gui's mother first conceived him, she dreamed that an old man handed her a child, saying, "I give you this child, that he may live long and attain high rank."

sentences.zh: 及生，形類所夢，故以永貴字之。

translations.literal: When he was born, his form resembled the child in the dream, and so he was given the style Yonggui.
translations.idiomatic: When he was born, he resembled the child in the dream, and so was given the courtesy name Yonggui.

sentences.zh: 貴少從師受學，嘗輟書歎曰：「男兒當提劍汗馬以取公侯，何能為博士也！」

translations.literal: Gui from youth studied under teachers; once he put down his books and sighed: "A man should take sword in hand and horse under him to win noble rank—how can he become a scholar!"
translations.idiomatic: Gui studied under teachers from youth, but once he put down his books and sighed, "A man should take sword in hand and horse under him to win noble rank. How can he become a mere scholar!"

sentences.zh: 魏正光末，破六韓拔陵圍夏州，刺史源子邕嬰城固守，以貴為統軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguang under Wei, Poliuhan Baling besieged Xia Province; Governor Yuan Ziyong held the city in defense and made Gui a commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenguang era under Wei, Poliuhan Baling besieged Xia Province; Governor Yuan Ziyong held the city and appointed Gui a commander.

sentences.zh: 後從爾硃榮禽葛榮於滏口，加別將。

translations.literal: Later he followed Erzhu Rong in capturing Ge Rong at Fukou and was promoted to separate commander.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Erzhu Rong in capturing Ge Rong at Fukou and was promoted to separate commander.

sentences.zh: 又從元天穆平邢杲，轉都督。

translations.literal: He also followed Yuan Tianmu in pacifying Xing Gao and was transferred to commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Yuan Tianmu in pacifying Xing Gao and was made commandant.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，貴率鄉兵從爾硃榮有功，封革融縣侯。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Gui led local troops under Erzhu Rong with merit and was enfeoffed Marquis of Gerong County.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Gui led local troops under Erzhu Rong with distinction and was enfeoffed Marquis of Gerong County.

sentences.zh: 除郢州刺史，入為武衛將軍、關內大都督。

translations.literal: He was made Governor of Ying Province, then entered court as General of the Martial Guard and Grand Commandant of Guannei.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Ying Province, then entered court as General of the Martial Guard and Grand Commandant of Guannei.

sentences.zh: 從魏孝武西遷，進爵化政郡公。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei in the western move and was advanced to Duke of Huazheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei in the move west and was enfeoffed Duke of Huazheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 貴善騎射，有將帥才。

translations.literal: Gui was skilled in horsemanship and archery and possessed the talent of a general.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was skilled in horsemanship and archery and had the talent of a commander.

sentences.zh: 周文帝又以宗室，甚親委之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou, because he was of the imperial clan, also trusted and relied on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou also trusted him deeply because he was a member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 大統初，與獨孤信入洛陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong he entered Luoyang with Dugu Xin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Datong he entered Luoyang with Dugu Xin.

sentences.zh: 東魏潁州長史賀若統據潁川來降，東魏遣將堯雄、趙育、是雲寶率眾二萬攻潁川。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Chief Clerk of Ying Province He Ruo Tong held Yingchuan and submitted; Eastern Wei sent generals Yao Xiong, Zhao Yu, and Shiyun Bao with twenty thousand men to attack Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruo Tong, chief clerk of Ying Province under Eastern Wei, held Yingchuan and submitted; Eastern Wei sent generals Yao Xiong, Zhao Yu, and Shiyun Bao with twenty thousand men against Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 貴自洛陽率步騎二千救之，軍次陽翟。

translations.literal: Gui led two thousand infantry and cavalry from Luoyang to rescue them and halted at Yangdi.
translations.idiomatic: Gui led two thousand infantry and cavalry from Luoyang to the rescue and halted at Yangdi.

sentences.zh: 雄等去潁川四十里，東魏行台任祥又率眾四萬，將與雄合。

translations.literal: Xiong and the others were forty li from Yingchuan; Eastern Wei Commissioner Ren Xiang also led forty thousand men and was about to join Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong and the others were forty li from Yingchuan; Eastern Wei Commissioner Ren Xiang also led forty thousand men and was about to join them.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸以彼眾我寡，不可爭鋒。

translations.literal: The generals all thought the enemy numerous and themselves few and that they should not contend.
translations.idiomatic: The generals all argued that the enemy outnumbered them and that they should not give battle.

sentences.zh: 貴曰：「若賀若一陷，吾輩坐此何為？」

translations.literal: Gui said: "If He Ruo falls, what are we sitting here for?"
translations.idiomatic: Gui said, "If He Ruo falls, what are we doing sitting here?"

sentences.zh: 遂入潁川。

translations.literal: He thereupon entered Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched into Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 雄等稍進，貴率千人背城為陣，與雄合戰。

translations.literal: Xiong and the others advanced gradually; Gui led a thousand men with their backs to the city in battle array and joined combat with Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong and the others advanced; Gui led a thousand men with their backs to the city wall and engaged Xiong in battle.

sentences.zh: 貴馬中流矢，乃短兵步鬥，雄大敗輕走，趙育於是降。

translations.literal: Gui's horse was struck by a stray arrow; he then fought on foot with short weapons; Xiong was routed and fled lightly, and Zhao Yu thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's horse was struck by a stray arrow; he fought on foot with short weapons; Xiong was routed and fled, and Zhao Yu surrendered.

sentences.zh: 任祥聞雄敗，遂不敢進。

translations.literal: When Ren Xiang heard that Xiong had been defeated, he dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren Xiang heard of Xiong's defeat, he dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 貴乘勝逼祥，敗之。

translations.literal: Gui pressed his victory against Xiang and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui pressed his victory against Xiang and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 是雲寶亦降。

translations.literal: Shiyun Bao also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyun Bao also surrendered.

sentences.zh: 師還。

translations.literal: The army returned.
translations.idiomatic: The army returned.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝在天遊園，以金卮置侯上，令公卿射中者即賜之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei was at the Tianyou Garden; he placed a golden goblet on a target and ordered that whichever minister hit it should receive it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei was at the Tianyou Garden; he placed a golden goblet on a target and promised it to whichever minister hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 貴一發而中。

translations.literal: Gui hit it with a single shot.
translations.idiomatic: Gui hit it on the first shot.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「由基之妙，正當爾耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "The skill of Yang Youji is just like this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "The skill of Yang Youji is exactly like this."

sentences.zh: 進侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Master of the Office with the same ceremonial rank as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Master of the Office equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遷中外府左長史，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to Left Chief Clerk of the Central and Outer Office and advanced to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to Left Chief Clerk of the Central and Outer Office and promoted to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 宕昌王梁彌定為宗人獠甘所逐，來奔。
