translations.literal: Liang Miding, King of Dangchang, was driven out by his clansman the Liao chief Gan and came in flight to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Miding, King of Dangchang, was driven out by his clansman, the tribal chief Gan, and fled to submit.

sentences.zh: 又有羌酋傍乞鐵忽，因梁ＧＣ定反後，據有渠株川，擁隸數千家，與渭州人鄭五醜同反。

translations.literal: There was also the Qiang chieftain Pangqi Tiehu, who after Miding's rebellion held Qizhu Valley, controlled several thousand households, and rebelled together with Zheng Wuchou of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Qiang chieftain Pangqi Tiehu, who after Miding's rebellion held Qizhu Valley, controlled several thousand households, and rebelled together with Zheng Wuchou of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 周文令貴與豆盧甯、史寧討之，貴等禽斬鐵忽及五醜，史寧又別擊獠甘破之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou ordered Gui with Doulu Ning and Shi Ning to attack them; Gui and the others captured and beheaded Tiehu and Wuchou, and Shi Ning separately attacked and defeated the Liao chief Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou ordered Gui, Doulu Ning, and Shi Ning to suppress them; Gui and the others captured and killed Tiehu and Wuchou, and Shi Ning separately defeated the tribal chief Gan.

sentences.zh: 乃納彌定，並于渠株川置岷州。

translations.literal: They then received Miding and established Min Province at Qizhu Valley.
translations.idiomatic: They then received Miding and established Min Province at Qizhu Valley.

sentences.zh: 朝廷重功，遂於粟阪立碑，以紀其績。

translations.literal: The court valued their merit and erected a stele at Suban to record their achievements.
translations.idiomatic: The court honored their achievements and erected a stele at Suban to commemorate them.

sentences.zh: 廢帝三年，詔貴代尉遲迥鎮蜀。

translations.literal: In the third year of Emperor Fei, an edict ordered Gui to replace Yuchi Jiong as commander in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Emperor Fei, an edict ordered Gui to replace Yuchi Jiong as commander in Shu.

sentences.zh: 時隆州人開府李光易反於鹽亭，攻圍隆州；

translations.literal: At the time Li Guangyi of Longzhou, a Grand Master of the Office, rebelled at Yanting and besieged Longzhou;
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Guangyi of Longzhou, a Grand Master of the Office, rebelled at Yanting and besieged Longzhou;

sentences.zh: 而隆州人李拓亦聚眾反，開府張道應之。

translations.literal: Li Tuo of Longzhou also gathered a host and rebelled, and Grand Master of the Office Zhang Dao joined him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tuo of Longzhou also gathered followers and rebelled, and Grand Master of the Office Zhang Dao joined him.

sentences.zh: 貴乃命開府叱奴與牧隆州，又令開府成亞擊拓及道降之，並送京師。

translations.literal: Gui then ordered Grand Master of the Office Chinu to guard Longzhou, and also ordered Grand Master of the Office Cheng Ya to attack Tuo and Dao, reduce them, and send them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Gui ordered Grand Master of the Office Chinu to guard Longzhou and Grand Master of the Office Cheng Ya to attack Tuo and Dao, subdue them, and send them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 除益州刺史，未就拜小司徒。

translations.literal: He was made Governor of Yi Province but before taking office was appointed Junior Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Yi Province but before taking office was made Junior Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 先是蜀人多劫盜，貴乃召任俠傑健者署為遊軍二十四部，令其督捕，由是頗息。

translations.literal: Previously the people of Shu were much given to robbery; Gui then summoned bold and able men of chivalry and appointed them to twenty-four patrol units to supervise arrests, and from this the trouble largely ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the people of Shu were much given to robbery; Gui summoned bold and able men and appointed them to twenty-four patrol units to hunt down bandits, and the trouble largely ceased.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，進位柱國，拜禦正中大。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, Gui was advanced to Pillar of the State and appointed Grand Master of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, Gui was promoted to Pillar of the State and appointed Grand Master of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 武成初，與賀蘭祥討吐谷渾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng he campaigned against Tuyuhun with Helan Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wucheng era he campaigned against Tuyuhun with Helan Xiang.

sentences.zh: 軍還，進封許國公、邑萬戶，舊爵回封一子。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was advanced to Duke of Xu with a fief of ten thousand households, and his former title was transferred to one son.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was enfeoffed Duke of Xu with a fief of ten thousand households, and his former title was transferred to one son.

sentences.zh: 遷大司空，行小塚宰，曆大司徒，遷太保。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Minister of Works, acted as Junior Minister of State, served as Grand Minister over the Masses, and was transferred to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Grand Minister of Works, acting Junior Minister of State, then Grand Minister over the Masses, and finally Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 貴好音樂，耽奕棋，留連不倦。

translations.literal: Gui loved music and was absorbed in chess, lingering without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Gui loved music and was absorbed in chess, lingering over them tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 然好施愛士，時人頗以此稱之。

translations.literal: Yet he was generous and loved scholars, and people of the time praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was generous and loved men of talent, and people of the time praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 保定末，使突厥，迎皇后。

translations.literal: At the end of Baoding he was sent to the Turks to escort the empress.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Baoding he was sent to the Turks to escort the empress back.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，還至張掖，薨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe, on returning to Zhangye, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianhe he died on returning to Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Mu.

sentences.zh: 子善嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 善紘厚有武藝。

translations.literal: Shan was generous and possessed martial skill.
translations.idiomatic: Shan was generous and possessed martial skill.

sentences.zh: 大象末位上柱國，封許國公。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang he held the rank of Upper Pillar of the State and was enfeoffed Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang era he held the rank of Upper Pillar of the State and was enfeoffed Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，遇之甚厚，拜其子穎上儀同。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui accepted the abdication, he treated Shan very generously and appointed his son Ying Upper Master of the Same Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui accepted the throne, he treated Shan very generously and appointed his son Ying Upper Master of the Same Rank.

sentences.zh: 及善弟忻誅，並廢於家。

translations.literal: When Shan's younger brother Xin was executed, both were stripped of office and confined at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Shan's younger brother Xin was executed, both were stripped of office and confined at home.

sentences.zh: 善未幾卒。

translations.literal: Shan died not long after.
translations.idiomatic: Shan died soon after.

sentences.zh: 穎，大業中，位司農少卿，後沒李密。

translations.literal: Ying, during Daye, held the post of Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture and later perished under Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Ying, during the Daye era, served as Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture and later died in Li Mi's service.

sentences.zh: 善弟忻。

translations.literal: Shan's younger brother Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Shan's younger brother was Xin.

sentences.zh: 忻字仲樂，幼而敏慧，為童兒時，與群輩戲，輒為部伍，進止行列，無不用命者。

translations.literal: Xin, styled Zhongle, was clever from childhood; as a boy, when playing with his companions he would always organize them into ranks, and in advancing, halting, and forming lines none failed to obey.
translations.idiomatic: Xin, courtesy name Zhongle, was clever from childhood. As a boy, when playing with companions he would organize them into ranks, and in marching, halting, and forming lines none failed to obey.

sentences.zh: 年十二，能左右馳射，驍捷若飛。

translations.literal: At twelve he could shoot while riding to either side, swift and agile as flight.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he could shoot while riding to either side, swift and agile as a bird in flight.

sentences.zh: 恆謂所親曰：「自古名將，唯以韓、白、衛、霍為美談，吾察其行事，未足多尚，使與僕並時，不令豎子獨擅高名。」

translations.literal: He often said to those close to him: "Famous generals of old are praised only for Han, Bai, Wei, and Huo; examining their deeds, they are not greatly admirable—if they had lived in my time, I would not let those fellows monopolize high fame."
translations.idiomatic: He often told those close to him, "Famous generals of old are praised only for Han Xin, Bai Qi, Wei Qing, and Huo Qubing. Examining their deeds, I find little to admire. Had they lived in my time, I would not let those fellows monopolize fame."

sentences.zh: 年十八，從周齊王憲討突厥，以功拜儀同三司，賜爵興固縣公。

translations.literal: At eighteen he followed Prince of Qi Xian of Zhou in campaigning against the Turks and for his merit was appointed Master of the Same Rank as the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed Duke of Xinggu County.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he followed Prince of Qi Xian of Zhou against the Turks and for his achievements was appointed Master of the Same Rank as the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed Duke of Xinggu County.

sentences.zh: 韋孝寬以忻驍勇，請與鎮玉壁，以戰功加開府，進爵化政郡公。

translations.literal: Wei Xiaokuan, because Xin was fierce and bold, requested that he garrison Yubi with him; for battle merit he was promoted to Grand Master of the Office and advanced to Duke of Huazheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xin was fierce and bold, Wei Xiaokuan asked him to garrison Yubi; for his battle achievements he was promoted to Grand Master of the Office and enfeoffed Duke of Huazheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 從武帝攻拔晉州。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Wu in capturing Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu in capturing Jin Province.

sentences.zh: 齊後主親總兵，六軍憚之，欲旋。

translations.literal: The Later Lord of Qi personally commanded the army; the six armies feared him and wished to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord of Qi personally commanded the army; the six armies feared him and wished to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 忻諫曰：「以陛下之聖武，乘敵人之荒縱，何往而不克？

translations.literal: Xin remonstrated, saying: "With Your Majesty's sage martial prowess, riding the enemy's dissolute neglect, where could you not conquer?
translations.idiomatic: Xin remonstrated, "With Your Majesty's sage martial prowess, taking advantage of the enemy's dissolute neglect, where could you not conquer?

sentences.zh: 若齊人更得令主，君臣協力，未易平也。」

translations.literal: If Qi should again obtain a worthy ruler and ruler and ministers cooperate, it would not be easy to pacify."
translations.idiomatic: If Qi should again obtain a worthy ruler and ruler and ministers cooperate, it will not be easy to conquer."

sentences.zh: 帝從之，乃戰，遂大克。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed, fought, and won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, gave battle, and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 及帝攻陷并州，先勝後敗。

translations.literal: When the emperor attacked and took Bing Province, he first won and then was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor attacked and took Bing Province, he first won and then was defeated.

sentences.zh: 帝為賊所窘，挺身而遁。

translations.literal: The emperor was hard pressed by the enemy and broke through alone to escape.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was hard pressed by the enemy and broke through alone to escape.

sentences.zh: 諸將多勸帝還，忻勃然曰：「破城士卒輕敵，微有不利，何足為懷？

translations.literal: Many generals urged the emperor to return; Xin angrily said: "The troops who took the city despise the enemy; a slight setback—what is there to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: Many generals urged the emperor to withdraw; Xin angrily said, "The troops who took the city despise the enemy. A slight setback is nothing to worry about.

sentences.zh: 今破竹形已成，奈何棄之而去！」

translations.literal: Now the bamboo-splitting momentum is formed—how can we abandon it and leave!"
translations.idiomatic: The momentum is like splitting bamboo—how can we abandon it now!"

sentences.zh: 帝納其言，明日復戰，拔晉陽。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words; the next day they fought again and took Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice; the next day they fought again and took Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 齊平，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: When Qi was pacified, he was advanced to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was pacified, he was promoted to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 尋與烏丸軌破陳將吳明徹于呂梁，進位柱國，除豫州總管。

translations.literal: Soon with Wuyuan Gui he defeated the Chen general Wu Mingche at Lüliang, was advanced to Pillar of the State, and was made Commander-in-Chief of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, with Wuyuan Gui, he defeated the Chen general Wu Mingche at Lüliang, was promoted to Pillar of the State, and was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝龍潛時，與忻情好甚協，及為丞相，恩顧彌隆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was still in obscurity, he and Xin were on very friendly terms; when he became Chancellor, his favor toward Xin grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was still in obscurity, he and Xin were close friends; when he became chancellor, his favor toward Xin grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥作亂，以忻為行軍總管，隋韋孝寬擊之。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, Xin was made Campaign Commander and followed Wei Xiaokuan of Sui in attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, Xin was made campaign commander and marched with Wei Xiaokuan of Sui against him.

sentences.zh: 時兵頓河陽，帝令高熲馳驛監軍，與穎密謀進取者，唯忻而已。

translations.literal: At the time the army halted at Heyang; the emperor sent Gao Jiong by post horse to supervise the army, and of those who secretly plotted advance with Jiong, only Xin was trusted.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Heyang; the emperor sent Gao Jiong by express relay to supervise the campaign, and of those who secretly plotted strategy with Jiong, only Xin was trusted.

sentences.zh: 迥遣子惇盛兵武陟，忻擊走之。

translations.literal: Jiong sent his son Dun with a strong force to Wuzhi; Xin attacked and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong sent his son Dun with a strong force to Wuzhi; Xin attacked and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 進臨相州，迥遣精甲三千伏野馬岡，忻以五百騎襲之，斬獲略盡。

translations.literal: Advancing to Xiang Province, Jiong sent three thousand elite armored troops to lie in ambush at Yema Hill; Xin with five hundred horsemen raided them and killed or captured nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Xiang Province, Jiong sent three thousand elite troops to ambush at Yema Hill; Xin with five hundred horsemen raided them and killed or captured nearly all.

sentences.zh: 進至草橋，迥又拒守，忻以奇兵破之，直趨鄴下。

translations.literal: Advancing to Caobridge, Jiong again held in defense; Xin broke him with surprise troops and drove straight toward Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Caobridge, Jiong again held the line; Xin broke through with a flanking force and drove straight toward Ye.

sentences.zh: 迥背城結陣，大戰，官軍不利。

translations.literal: Jiong formed battle lines with his back to the city; in the great battle the government army fared poorly.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong formed battle lines with his back to the city; in the great battle the government army fared poorly.

sentences.zh: 時鄴城士庶觀戰者數萬人，忻謂左右曰：「事急矣，吾當以權道破之。」

translations.literal: At the time tens of thousands of gentry and commoners of Ye watched the battle; Xin said to those beside him: "The situation is urgent; I shall use an expedient stratagem to break it."
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of people from Ye watched the battle; Xin told those beside him, "The situation is urgent. I shall use a stratagem to break it."

sentences.zh: 於是時觀者走之，轉相騰籍，聲如雷霆。

translations.literal: He then had the spectators run about; they trampled one another in turn, and the noise was like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: He then set the spectators running; they trampled one another, and the noise was like thunder.

sentences.zh: 忻乃傳呼曰：「賊敗矣」。

translations.literal: Xin then shouted through the crowd: "The rebels are defeated!"
translations.idiomatic: Xin then shouted through the crowd, "The rebels are defeated!"

sentences.zh: 眾復振，齊力急擊之，迥軍大敗。

translations.literal: The host rallied again, struck together with force, and Jiong's army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: The army rallied, struck together with renewed force, and Jiong's army was routed.

sentences.zh: 及平鄴，以功遷上柱國。

translations.literal: When Ye was pacified, he was transferred to Upper Pillar of the State for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye was pacified, he was promoted to Upper Pillar of the State for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 文帝謂「尉遲迥傾山東之眾，連百萬之師，公舉無遺算，策無全陣，誠天下英傑也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said: "Yuchi Jiong marshaled the hosts of Shandong and linked armies of a million; in your every move nothing was miscalculated, in your every plan no formation was left intact—you are truly a hero of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said, "Yuchi Jiong marshaled the hosts of Shandong and linked armies of a million. In your every move nothing was miscalculated, in your every plan no formation was left intact. You are truly a hero of the realm."

sentences.zh: 進封英國公。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Duke of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 自是每參帷幄，出入臥內，禪代之際，忻有力焉。

translations.literal: From then on he attended every council in the command tent, entering and leaving the inner quarters; at the time of the abdication transfer, Xin had a strong hand in it.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he attended every council in the command tent and entered the inner quarters; at the time of the dynastic transition, Xin played a major role.

sentences.zh: 後拜右領軍大將軍，寵顧彌重。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Right General of the Leading Army, and favor toward him grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Right General of the Leading Army, and imperial favor toward him grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 忻解兵法，馭戎齊整，當時六軍有一善事，雖非忻建，在下輒相謂曰：「此必英公法也。」

translations.literal: Xin understood military methods and kept troops in good order; whenever the six armies had some good practice, even if Xin had not instituted it, those below would say to one another: "This must be Duke of Ying's method."
translations.idiomatic: Xin understood military methods and kept troops in good order. Whenever the six armies adopted some good practice, even if Xin had not instituted it, the men would say, "That must be Duke of Ying's method."

sentences.zh: 其見推服如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 後改封祀國公。

translations.literal: Later his title was changed to Duke of Si.
translations.idiomatic: Later his title was changed to Duke of Si.

sentences.zh: 上嘗欲令忻擊突厥，高潁曰：「忻有異志，不可委以大兵。」

translations.literal: The emperor once wished to have Xin attack the Turks; Gao Jiong said: "Xin has rebellious intentions and cannot be entrusted with a great army."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once wished to send Xin against the Turks; Gao Jiong said, "Xin has rebellious intentions and cannot be entrusted with a great army."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 忻既佐命功臣，頻經將領，甚有威名，上由是微忌之，以譴去官。

translations.literal: Xin was a founding minister who had repeatedly held command and enjoyed great renown; the emperor therefore grew somewhat wary of him and removed him from office through censure.
translations.idiomatic: As a founding minister who had repeatedly held command and enjoyed great renown, Xin aroused the emperor's suspicion, and he was removed from office through censure.

sentences.zh: 與梁士彥昵狎，數相往來。

translations.literal: He was intimate with Liang Shiyan and visited one another frequently.
translations.idiomatic: He was on intimate terms with Liang Shiyan and visited him frequently.

sentences.zh: 士彥時亦怨望，陰圖不軌。

translations.literal: Shiyan was also resentful at the time and secretly plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan was also resentful at the time and secretly plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 忻謂士彥曰：「帝王豈有常乎？

translations.literal: Xin said to Shiyan: "Are emperors fixed forever?
translations.idiomatic: Xin said to Shiyan, "Are emperors fixed forever?

sentences.zh: 相扶即是。

translations.literal: Supporting one another is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Supporting one another is enough.

sentences.zh: 公于蒲州起事，我必從征，兩陣相當，然後中連結，天下可圖也。」

translations.literal: If you raise rebellion at Pu Province, I shall certainly join the campaign; when our two armies face each other, we can then join in the middle, and the realm may be taken."
translations.idiomatic: If you raise rebellion at Pu Province, I shall join the campaign. When our two armies face each other, we can link up in the middle, and the realm may be taken."

sentences.zh: 謀泄伏誅，家口籍沒。

translations.literal: The plot leaked and he was executed; his household and dependents were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The plot leaked and he was executed; his household and dependents were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 忻弟愷。

translations.literal: Xin's younger brother Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's younger brother was Kai.

sentences.zh: 愷字安樂，在周以功臣子，年三歲賜爵雙泉伯，七歲進封安平公。

translations.literal: Kai, styled Anle, as the son of a meritorious minister under Zhou, at three was granted the title Baron of Shuangquan and at seven was advanced to Duke of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: Kai, courtesy name Anle, as the son of a meritorious minister under Zhou, was granted the title Baron of Shuangquan at three and enfeoffed Duke of Anping at seven.

sentences.zh: 愷少有器局，諸兄並以弓馬自達，愷獨好學。

translations.literal: Kai from youth had breadth of vision; his elder brothers all distinguished themselves through archery and horsemanship, but Kai alone loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Kai from youth had breadth of vision. His elder brothers all distinguished themselves through archery and horsemanship, but Kai alone loved learning.

sentences.zh: 博覽書記，解文，多伎藝，為名公子。

translations.literal: He read widely in books and records, understood writing, and had many skills, and was acclaimed as a famous young nobleman.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in books and records, understood writing, and had many skills, and was acclaimed as a famous young nobleman.

sentences.zh: 累遷禦正中大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of the Imperial Household and Master of the Same Rank as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of the Imperial Household and Master of the Same Rank as the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，加上開府，近師中大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor, Kai was promoted to Upper Grand Master of the Office and Master of the Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chancellor, Kai was promoted to Upper Grand Master of the Office and Master of the Palace Attendants.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，誅宇文氏，愷亦將見殺，以與周本別，又兄忻有功，故見赦。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne and executed the Yuwen clan, Kai was also about to be killed, but because he was of a separate branch of Zhou and because his elder brother Xin had merit, he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ascended the throne and executed the Yuwen clan, Kai was also about to be killed, but because he was of a separate branch of Zhou and his elder brother Xin had rendered service, he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 後拜營宗廟副監、太子左庶子。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Deputy Supervisor of the Ancestral Temple Construction and Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Deputy Supervisor of the Ancestral Temple Construction and Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 廟成，別封甑山縣公。

translations.literal: When the temple was completed, he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Zengshan County.
translations.idiomatic: When the temple was completed, he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Zengshan County.

sentences.zh: 及遷都，上以愷有巧思，詔領營新都副監。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved, the emperor, because Kai had ingenious ideas, ordered him to supervise construction of the new capital as deputy supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was moved, the emperor, recognizing Kai's ingenuity, ordered him to serve as deputy supervisor of the new capital's construction.

sentences.zh: 高熲雖總大綱，凡所規畫，皆出於愷。

translations.literal: Although Gao Jiong held overall authority, every plan was Kai's.
translations.idiomatic: Although Gao Jiong held overall authority, every plan came from Kai.

sentences.zh: 及決渭水達河以通運漕，詔愷總督其事。

translations.literal: When the Wei River was diverted to reach the Yellow River for transport, an edict ordered Kai to supervise the project.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei River was diverted to reach the Yellow River for transport, an edict ordered Kai to supervise the project.

sentences.zh: 後拜萊州刺史，甚有能名。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Lai Province and gained a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Governor of Lai Province and gained a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 坐兄忻誅，除名於家，久不得調。

translations.literal: Because his elder brother Xin was executed, he was stripped of name and office and confined at home, and for a long time received no appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Because his elder brother Xin was executed, he was stripped of rank and confined at home, and for a long time received no appointment.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷以魯班故道，久絕不行，令愷修之。

translations.literal: It happened that the court, because the old road of Lu Ban had long been cut off and unused, ordered Kai to repair it.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Kai to repair the old Lu Ban road, which had long been cut off and unused.

sentences.zh: 既而上建仁壽宮，右僕射楊素言愷有巧思，於是檢校將作大匠。

translations.literal: Later the emperor built Renshou Palace; Right Manager Yang Su said that Kai had ingenious ideas, and so he was made acting Grand Artisan of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor built Renshou Palace, Right Manager Yang Su said Kai was ingenious, so Kai was made acting Grand Artisan of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜仁壽宮監，授儀同三司，尋為將作少監。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was appointed Supervisor of Renshou Palace and granted Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies; soon he became Junior Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year, he was appointed Supervisor of Renshou Palace and granted Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies; soon he became Junior Director of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 文獻皇后崩，愷與楊素營山陵。

translations.literal: When Empress Wenxian died, Kai and Yang Su constructed the mountain mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wenxian died, Kai and Yang Su oversaw construction of the mountain mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 上善之，復爵安平郡公。

translations.literal: The emperor approved of this and restored his title as Duke of Anping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and restored his title as Duke of Anping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，遷都洛陽，以愷為營東都副監，尋遷將作大匠。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne and moved the capital to Luoyang, he made Kai Deputy Supervisor for constructing the Eastern Capital; soon Kai was promoted to Grand Artisan of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne and moved the capital to Luoyang, Kai was made Deputy Supervisor for building the Eastern Capital and was soon promoted to Grand Artisan of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 愷揣帝心在宏侈，於是東都制度，窮極壯麗。

translations.literal: Kai surmised that the emperor’s heart was set on grandeur and extravagance, and so the design of the Eastern Capital exhausted magnificence and splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Kai understood that the emperor wanted grandeur and extravagance, so the Eastern Capital’s design was magnificent to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，進位開府，拜工部尚書。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, advanced him to Opening Office, and appointed him Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, promoted him to Opening Office, and appointed him Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 及長城之役，詔愷規度之。

translations.literal: When it came to the Great Wall labor service, an edict ordered Kai to plan and measure it.
translations.idiomatic: For the Great Wall project, an edict ordered Kai to survey and plan it.

sentences.zh: 時帝北巡，欲誇戎狄，令愷為大帳，其下坐數千人。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor toured north and wanted to impress the Rong and Di, so he ordered Kai to make a great tent beneath which several thousand people could sit.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured north and wanted to awe the northern peoples, he ordered Kai to make a great tent that could seat several thousand people underneath.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜物千段。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed one thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and bestowed one thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 又造觀風行殿，上容衛者數百人，離合為之，下施輪軸，推移倏忽，有若神功。

translations.literal: He also constructed the mobile Hall for Observing Customs; above it could hold several hundred guards, it could separate and join together, and below it had wheels and axles, so that it moved in an instant, as if by divine workmanship.
translations.idiomatic: He also built the mobile Hall for Observing Customs, which could hold several hundred guards above, separate and join together, and move instantly on wheels and axles below, as if made by divine craft.

sentences.zh: 戎狄見之，莫不驚駭。

translations.literal: When the Rong and Di saw it, none were not astonished and frightened.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern peoples saw it, they were all astonished and awed.

sentences.zh: 帝彌悅，前後賞賜不可勝紀。

translations.literal: The emperor was even more pleased, and the rewards bestowed before and after could not all be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still more pleased, and the rewards he gave Kai over time were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 是時將復古制明堂，議者皆不能決。

translations.literal: At that time they wished to restore the ancient Bright Hall system, and those debating it could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: At that time they wished to restore the ancient Bright Hall system, and the debaters could not reach a decision.

sentences.zh: 愷博考群籍，為明堂圖樣奏之。

translations.literal: Kai examined many texts and submitted a diagram of the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Kai examined many texts and submitted a diagram of the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 又以「張衡渾象用三分為一度，裴秀輿地以一寸為千里，臣之此圖以一分為一尺，推而演之」。

translations.literal: He also wrote: "Zhang Heng's armillary sphere uses one degree for every three parts; Pei Xiu's map of the land uses one inch for a thousand li; in my diagram one part equals one chi, extended and calculated accordingly."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Zhang Heng's armillary sphere uses one degree for every three parts; Pei Xiu's map of the land uses one inch for a thousand li; in my diagram one part equals one chi, extended and calculated accordingly."

sentences.zh: 又引于時議者，或以綺井為重屋，或以圓楣為隆棟，將為臆說，事不經見。

translations.literal: He also cited contemporary debaters, some of whom took patterned ceiling wells for double-roofed halls, or round lintels for lofty beams, as speculative talk unsupported by evidence.
translations.idiomatic: He also cited contemporary debaters, some of whom took patterned ceiling wells for double-roofed halls or round lintels for lofty beams as speculative talk unsupported by evidence.

sentences.zh: 今錄其疑難，為之通釋，皆出證據，以相發明。

translations.literal: Now recording their doubts and difficulties, he explained them, all with evidence to illuminate one another.
translations.idiomatic: He now recorded their doubts and difficulties and explained them, all with evidence to illuminate one another.

sentences.zh: 為議曰：

translations.literal: His memorial states:
translations.idiomatic: His memorial states:

sentences.zh: 臣愷謹按《淮南子》曰：「昔者神農之禦天下也，甘雨以時，五穀蕃植，春生夏長，秋收冬藏，月省時考，終歲獻貢，以時嘗谷，祀於明堂。

translations.literal: Your subject Kai respectfully notes the Huainanzi: "In antiquity when Shennong ruled the realm, timely sweet rain fell, the five grains flourished, spring begot and summer grew, autumn harvested and winter stored; at each month and season he examined affairs, and at year's end tribute was presented; at the proper season grain was tasted and sacrifice was offered in the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Kai respectfully notes the Huainanzi: "In antiquity when Shennong ruled the realm, timely sweet rain fell, the five grains flourished, spring begot and summer grew, autumn harvested and winter stored; at each month and season he examined affairs, and at year's end tribute was presented; at the proper season grain was tasted and sacrifice was offered in the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 明堂之制，有蓋而無四方，風雨不能襲，燥濕不能傷，遷延而入之。」

translations.literal: The form of the Bright Hall had a covering but no four sides; wind and rain could not penetrate, dryness and damp could not harm it, and one entered by a winding approach."
translations.idiomatic: The form of the Bright Hall had a covering but no four sides; wind and rain could not penetrate, dryness and damp could not harm it, and one entered by a winding approach."

sentences.zh: 臣愷以為上古樸略，創立典刑。

translations.literal: Your subject Kai considers that in high antiquity things were plain and simple, and institutions were first established.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Kai considers that in high antiquity things were plain and simple, and institutions were first established.

sentences.zh: 《尚書帝命驗》曰：「帝者承天，立五府以尊天重象，赤曰文祖，黃曰神鬥，白曰顯紀，黑曰玄矩，蒼曰靈府。」

translations.literal: The Apocryphal Documents on the Mandate of the Emperor states: "The emperor receives Heaven and establishes the Five Offices to honor Heaven and respect the celestial signs: the red is Wen Zu, the yellow is Shen Dou, the white is Xian Ji, the black is Xuan Ju, and the green is Ling Fu."
translations.idiomatic: The Apocryphal Documents on the Mandate of the Emperor states: "The emperor receives Heaven and establishes the Five Offices to honor Heaven and respect the celestial signs: the red is Wen Zu, the yellow is Shen Dou, the white is Xian Ji, the black is Xuan Ju, and the green is Ling Fu."

sentences.zh: 注云：「唐虞之天府，夏之世室，殷之重屋，周之明堂，皆同矣。」

translations.literal: The commentary states: "The Celestial Treasury of Tang and Yu, the World Chamber of Xia, the Double Roof of Yin, and the Bright Hall of Zhou are all the same."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary states: "The Celestial Treasury of Tang and Yu, the World Chamber of Xia, the Double Roof of Yin, and the Bright Hall of Zhou are all the same."

sentences.zh: 《屍子》曰：「有虞氏曰總章。」

translations.literal: The Shizi states: "The Youyu clan called it Zong Zhang."
translations.idiomatic: The Shizi states: "The Youyu clan called it Zong Zhang."

sentences.zh: 《周官考工記》曰：「夏後氏世室，堂修二七，博四修一。」

translations.literal: The Artificers' Record in the Offices of Zhou states: "The World Chamber of the Xia had a hall depth of two sevens and a width of one fourth beyond four times the depth."
translations.idiomatic: The Artificers' Record in the Offices of Zhou states: "The World Chamber of the Xia had a hall depth of two sevens and a width of one fourth beyond four times the depth."

sentences.zh: 注云：「修，南北之深也。

translations.literal: The commentary states: "Depth is the north-south measurement.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary states: "Depth is the north-south measurement.

sentences.zh: 夏度以步，合堂修十四步，其博益以四分修之一，則堂博十七步半也。」

translations.literal: The Xia foot-measure being in paces, the hall depth would be fourteen paces; adding one fourth of four times the depth to the width gives a hall width of seventeen and a half paces."
translations.idiomatic: The Xia foot-measure being in paces, the hall depth would be fourteen paces; adding one fourth of four times the depth to the width gives a hall width of seventeen and a half paces."

sentences.zh: 臣愷案：三王之世，夏最為古，從質尚文，理應漸就寬大，何因夏室乃大殷堂？

translations.literal: Your subject Kai notes: among the Three Dynasties Xia is most ancient; moving from substance toward refinement, reason would gradually broaden—why then was the Xia chamber larger than the Yin hall?
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Kai notes: among the Three Dynasties Xia is most ancient; moving from substance toward refinement, reason would gradually broaden—why then was the Xia chamber larger than the Yin hall?

sentences.zh: 相形為論，理恐不爾。
